title: God Creates Everything From Scratch
paragraphs: § Day 1: Let There Be Light!

Alright, so here's the deal. First thing, God created the heavens and the earth—everything you see and everything you don't. At the beginning, the earth was just a formless, empty void, totally dark and chaotic. God's Spirit was just hovering over the waters like a bird. Then God said, "Light!" and boom, light appeared. God saw the light was awesome, so He separated the light from the darkness. He named the light "Day" and the darkness "Night." Evening passed and morning came—that was day one. Legendary, right?
§ Day 2: Making the Sky

Then God said, "Let there be a sky in the middle of the waters to separate water from water!" So God made the sky and separated the water under the sky from the water above it. And it happened just like that. God called the sky "heaven." Evening passed and morning came—that was day two.
§ Day 3: Land and Plants Appear

God then said, "Let the water under the sky be gathered into one place, and let dry ground appear!" And it happened. God called the dry ground "land," and the gathered waters He called "seas." And God saw that it was good. Then He said, "Let the land produce vegetation: seed-bearing plants and trees on the land that bear fruit with seed in it, according to their various kinds!" And the land produced all sorts of plants and trees. God saw that it was totally good. Evening passed and morning came—that was day three.
§ Day 4: Sun, Moon, and Stars

God said, "Let there be lights in the sky to separate the day from the night, and let them serve as signs to mark seasons and days and years. Let them be lights in the sky to give light on the earth!" And it happened. God made two great lights—the greater light to govern the day and the lesser light to govern the night. He also made the stars. God set them in the sky to light up the earth and to govern the day and the night, separating light from darkness. And God saw that it was totally good. Evening passed and morning came—that was day four.
§ Day 5: Fish and Birds

God said, "Let the water teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the vault of the sky!" So God created the great creatures of the sea and every living thing with which the water teems and that moves about in it, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that it was good. God blessed them and said, "Be fruitful and increase in number and fill the water in the seas, and let the birds increase on the earth!" Evening passed and morning came—that was day five.
§ Day 6: Animals and Humans

God said, "Let the land produce living creatures according to their kinds: the livestock, the creatures that move along the ground, and the wild animals, each according to its kind!" And it was so. God made the wild animals, the livestock, and all the creatures that move along the ground. And God saw that it was good. Then God said, "Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness, so that they may rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, over the livestock and all the wild animals, and over all the creatures that move along the ground." So God created mankind in his own image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them. God blessed them and said to them, "Be fruitful and increase in number; fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky and over every living creature that moves on the ground." Then God said, "I give you every seed-bearing plant on the face of the whole earth and every tree that has fruit with seed in it. They will be yours for food. And to all the beasts of the earth and all the birds in the sky and all the creatures that move along the ground—everything that has the breath of life in it—I give every green plant for food." And it was so. God saw all that he had made, and it was very, very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day. How cool is that?

title: God Creates a Helper for Adam
paragraphs: So, the universe and our world were totally complete, like, every single detail was done.

By day seven, God had finished everything He was doing. So on the seventh day, He just chilled and took a break from all His work. God gave the seventh day a special shout-out and made it holy, because that was the day He rested from all the creating He had been doing. This is the story of how it all began, how the heavens and the earth were created.
§ Adam and Eve

Back when God made the earth and the heavens, there were no plants or anything growing yet. That’s because God hadn't sent any rain, and there was no one to even farm the land. The whole planet was watered by these underground springs. Then, God took some dirt from the ground, shaped it into a man, and breathed life into him. And just like that, the man became a living person!

Then God planted this awesome garden in a place called Eden, out in the east. He put the man He had just made in it. God made all sorts of cool trees grow there—trees that were nice to look at and had delicious fruit. In the middle of the garden was the Tree of Life, and also the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil.

A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and it split into four smaller rivers. The first one is called the Pishon, and it flows through a land called Havilah, which has gold. The gold there is legit good. That land is also known for some sweet-smelling stuff and a cool stone called onyx. The second river is the Gihon, which flows through the land of Cush. The third river is the Hiddekel, and it runs east of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and keep it in good shape.

God gave the man a command, “You can eat from any tree in the garden, for real. But, you can’t eat from the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil. Don’t do it. The second you eat from that tree, you’re dead. Seriously.”

God said, “It’s not good for the man to be all by himself. I’ll make him a helper, a real partner.” So God made all the animals and birds out of the ground. He brought them to the man to see what he would name them. Whatever the man called each creature, that was its name. The man gave names to all the cattle, the birds, and the wild animals, but he still couldn’t find a good partner for himself.
So God made the man fall into a super deep sleep. While he was sleeping, God took out one of his ribs and patched him up. Then God used that rib to make a woman and brought her to the man.

The man was like, “Whoa, finally! She’s like me, bone of my bone, flesh of my flesh! I’ll call her Woman, because she was made from Man.” That’s why a man leaves his parents and sticks with his wife, and they become one. The two of them, the man and his wife, were both naked, but they weren’t embarrassed or anything.

title: The Mistake That Changed Everything
paragraphs: § The First Lie
So, get this: the snake was the craftiest of all the wild animals God had made. He slithered up to the woman and was like, "Yo, did God really say you can't eat from any of the trees in the garden?"

The woman shot back, "Nah, that's not it. We can totally eat from the trees in the garden. It's just that one tree in the middle. God was like, 'Don't eat from it, don't even touch it, or you'll die.'"

The snake hissed, "Pfft, you're not gonna die. God's just saying that because he knows the second you eat it, your eyes will be opened. You'll be like God, knowing everything from good to evil. Total game-changer."
§ The Big Mistake

The woman looked at the tree and saw that the fruit looked delicious. Plus, the idea of knowing everything was super tempting. So she took a bite and gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it too.
Instantly, it was like a filter came off. They saw everything, including the fact that they were totally naked! They scrambled to sew some fig leaves together for some makeshift clothes.
Later, they heard God strolling through the garden in the cool evening breeze, and they freaked out and hid in the trees.
God called out, "Where are you?"
The man answered, "I heard you in the garden, and I was scared because I was naked, so I hid."
God asked, "Who told you that you were naked? Did you eat from that tree I specifically told you not to eat from?"
The man said, "The woman you gave me, she gave me the fruit, and yeah, I ate it."
Then God said to the woman, "What have you done?"
She said, "The snake tricked me, and I ate it."
§ The Consequences

God said to the snake, "Because you did this, you're cursed. More cursed than any other animal. You'll crawl on your belly and eat dirt for the rest of your life. I'm putting a huge beef between you and the woman, and between your kids and her kids. He'll crush your head, and you'll strike his heel."
To the woman, he said, "Giving birth is going to be super painful. You'll have your babies in pain. You'll want to be close to your husband, but he'll be the boss of you."

To the man, he said, "Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree I commanded you not to, the ground is now cursed because of you. Getting food from it will be a huge struggle for the rest of your life. It'll grow thorns and weeds, and you'll have to sweat and work your butt off just to eat, until you die and go back to the ground you came from. You started as dust, and you'll end up as dust."
§ Kicked Out
The man, Adam, named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of everyone.
And God made them some better clothes out of leather and dressed them.
Then God said, "Wow, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. We can't let him reach out and eat from the Tree-of-Life and live forever. That can't happen."

So God kicked them out of the Garden of Eden. He sent them out to farm the land they were made from. He threw them out and put powerful angels and a flaming, spinning sword to the east of the garden to guard the way to the Tree-of-Life.

title: The First Murder and Its Epic Consequences
paragraphs: So, Adam and Eve got together, and soon enough, Eve was pregnant and had a baby boy named Cain. She was like, 'OMG, I made a person, with God's help!' After that, she had another son, Abel. Abel grew up to be a shepherd, taking care of sheep, while Cain was a farmer.
§ The First Sibling Rivalry

After a while, it was time to give offerings to God. Cain, being a farmer, brought some of his crops. Abel brought the best cuts of meat from his firstborn lambs. God was really happy with Abel's gift, but not so much with Cain's. Cain got super mad and threw a major fit.

God asked Cain, 'Yo, what's with the attitude? Why the long face? If you do the right thing, you'll be fine. But if you don't, sin is like a predator waiting to jump you. It's after you, but you have to be the one in control.'
Cain talked to his brother Abel. While they were out in the field, Cain attacked Abel and killed him.
§ The Cover-Up Fail
God asked Cain, 'Where's your brother Abel?'
He shot back, 'How am I supposed to know? Am I my brother's babysitter or something?'

God said, 'What did you do?! Your brother's blood is screaming to me from the ground. And now, you're cursed. The ground that soaked up your brother's blood won't grow anything for you anymore. You're going to be a homeless wanderer on this planet.'

Cain told God, 'This is too much! I can't handle this punishment. You're kicking me off my land, and I can't even face you. I'll be a homeless wanderer, and anyone who finds me will probably kill me.'
But God told him, 'Nah. Anyone who kills you will get it back seven times worse.' Then God put a special mark on Cain so that no one would kill him on sight.
So Cain left God's presence and went to live in the Land of Nod, which is east of Eden.
§ Cain's Family Line
Cain and his wife had a kid named Enoch. Cain then built a city and named it Enoch after his son. Enoch had a son named Irad, Irad had Mehujael, Mehujael had Methushael, and Methushael had Lamech.

Lamech married two women, Adah and Zillah. Adah had a son named Jabal, who was the OG of everyone who lives in tents and raises livestock. His brother was Jubal, the ancestor of all musicians who play the harp and flute. Zillah had a son named Tubal-Cain, who was a master blacksmith, making all sorts of bronze and iron tools. His sister was Naamah.
Lamech said to his wives, 'Adah and Zillah, listen up! I killed a guy for hurting me, a young dude who attacked me. If Cain gets avenged seven times, then for me, it's seventy-seven times!'
§ A New Hope

Adam and Eve got together again, and she had another son named Seth. She said, 'God has given me another child to replace Abel, since Cain killed him.' Seth also had a son, and he named him Enosh. It was around this time that people started to seriously pray and worship God.

title: Adam's Family Tree: The Road to Noah
paragraphs: § Adam's Family Tree

Here's the official family tree for the human race. When God created people, he made them in his own image, basically like a reflection of himself. He created them male and female, gave them a shout-out, and named the whole crew 'Humanity.'

When Adam was 130, he had a son who was his spitting image, a total mini-me, and he named him Seth. After Seth came along, Adam lived for another 800 years and had a bunch more sons and daughters. All in all, Adam lived for 930 years. And then he died.
When Seth was 105, he had a son named Enosh. After Enosh was born, Seth stuck around for another 807 years, having more kids. Seth lived for a grand total of 912 years. And then he died.
When Enosh was 90, he had Kenan. After Kenan, he lived for another 815 years, having more sons and daughters. Enosh made it to 905 years old. And then he died.
When Kenan was 70, he had Mahalalel. After Mahalalel, he was around for another 840 years, having more kids. Kenan lived a total of 910 years. And then he died.
When Mahalalel was 65, he had Jared. After Jared, he lived for another 830 years, with more sons and daughters. Mahalalel lived a total of 895 years. And then he died.
When Jared was 162, he had Enoch. After Enoch, he lived for another 800 years, having more kids. Jared lived a total of 962 years. And then he died.
§ The Guy Who Just Vanished

When Enoch was 65, he had Methuselah. Enoch was super tight with God, like they walked together all the time. After Methuselah was born, Enoch lived another 300 years, having more sons and daughters. Enoch lived for 365 years in total. He was always walking with God, and then one day—poof! He was just gone. God had beamed him up.
When Methuselah was 187, he had Lamech. After Lamech, he lived for another 782 years. Methuselah lived to be 969 years old. And then he died.

When Lamech was 182, he had a son. He named him Noah, saying, 'This kid is gonna give us a break from all this back-breaking work on the ground that God cursed.' After Noah was born, Lamech lived for another 595 years, having more sons and daughters. Lamech lived a total of 777 years. And then he died.
By the time Noah was 500, he had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

title: God's Epic Reset and Noah's Big Project
paragraphs: § The World Goes Wild
So, people started spreading all over the planet, and a ton of girls were born. Then, the "sons of God" saw how beautiful the human girls were and just started picking out wives for themselves.
But God was like, "Yo, I'm not gonna keep people alive forever. They're mortal, and from now on, they'll only live about 120 years."

Back then, there were actual giants roaming the Earth. These giants were the kids of the "sons of God" and human women. They were like the legendary heroes you hear about in old stories, super famous and all that.
§ God's Regret

God looked down and saw that things were getting seriously out of control. People were just thinking up and doing messed-up stuff 24/7. It got so bad that God was actually sorry he ever made humans. It totally broke his heart.
So God said, "That's it, I'm wiping everything out. I'm hitting the fresh start on my whole creation—people, animals, bugs, birds, everything. I'm so done with all of it."
But Noah was different. God saw something in Noah that he liked.
§ Noah Gets a Mission
Here's the deal with Noah: he was a genuinely good guy, totally solid in his community. He was tight with God. Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

From God's perspective, the world had turned into a total dumpster fire. Violence was everywhere. God took one look and saw how messed up everything was. Everyone was corrupt, and it was like the whole world was rotten to the core.
So God told Noah, "It's the end for humanity. The world is a violent mess, and I'm about to do a total wipeout."

"I want you to build a huge boat out of teakwood. Make a bunch of rooms in it and cover the whole thing with tar, inside and out. Make it 450 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 45 feet high. Put a roof on it with an 18-inch window near the top. Add a door on the side and build three decks—a lower, middle, and upper level.
"Listen up, because I'm about to flood the entire Earth. Everything and everyone is going to be destroyed. Total annihilation.

"But I'm making a deal with you. You're going to get on that boat with your wife, your sons, and their wives. And you need to bring two of every living creature—a male and a female—on the boat with you to keep them safe. Two of every kind of bird, mammal, and reptile. You've gotta save them. Also, grab a ton of food, enough for you and all the animals."
And Noah did it. He did everything exactly as God told him to.

title: The Great Flood: God Hits Reset
paragraphs: Then God told Noah, “Alright, time to get on the ark, you and your whole family. Seriously, out of everyone around, you’re the only one who’s got their act together. You need to bring seven pairs of every ‘clean’ animal—a boy and a girl for each. For the ‘unclean’ animals, just one pair of each. And also grab seven pairs of every kind of bird, male and female, so they can keep their species going on Earth. In exactly seven days, I’m going to make it rain for 40 days and 40 nights straight. I’m about to wipe the slate clean and get rid of everything I’ve created.” And Noah, like a champ, did everything God told him to do.
§ The Flood Begins

Noah was 600 years old when the flood hit. He, his wife, his sons, and their wives all got on the ark to stay safe from the floodwaters. All the animals—clean and unclean, birds, and all the little crawly things—came to Noah and boarded the ark in pairs, a male and a female, just like God had ordered. Seven days later, the flood started for real.

On the 17th day of the second month of Noah’s 600th year, everything went down. All the underground water sources exploded, and it was like the sky’s windows were thrown wide open. The rain was insane, pouring down for 40 days and 40 nights without stopping.

On that exact day, Noah and his family—his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, his wife, and his sons' wives—all got on the ark. They brought every kind of animal with them: wild animals, farm animals, all the creatures that crawl on the ground, and every kind of bird. Every living thing that breathes came to Noah and got on the ark in pairs. A male and a female of every species came, just as God had commanded Noah. Then God himself shut the door behind them.
§ Total Wipeout

The flood kept going for 40 days. The water level just kept rising, lifting the ark way up high above the ground. The water got deeper and deeper until the ark was just floating on the surface. It got so bad that even the tallest mountains were completely underwater—the water was like 20 feet above the highest peaks. Everything died. Every single living thing that moved on the earth was gone. Birds, farm animals, wild animals, all the swarming creatures—gone. And all the people—gone too. Every living, breathing thing on dry land died. Only Noah and his crew on the ark made it.
The floodwaters stuck around, covering everything, for 150 days.

title: A Fresh Start After the Great Flood
paragraphs: Then God finally remembered Noah and all the wild and farm animals with him on the ark. He sent a wind to blow across the earth, and the floodwaters started to go down. The underground springs got plugged up, the sky-windows closed, and the rain stopped. Little by little, the water level dropped. After 150 days, the worst was over.
§The Water Goes Down

On the 17th day of the 7th month, the ark landed on the mountains of Ararat. The water kept receding until the 10th month, and on the first day of that month, the tops of the mountains finally appeared. Forty days later, Noah opened the window he had made in the ark.

He sent out a raven, which just flew back and forth until the water on the earth had dried up. Then he sent out a dove to see if the water had gone down, but the dove couldn't find a single spot to land because water still covered everything. So it came back, and Noah reached out, caught it, and brought it back inside.

He waited another seven days and sent the dove out again. This time, it came back in the evening holding a freshly picked olive leaf in its beak. That's how Noah knew the water was almost gone. He waited another seven days and sent the dove out a third time. This time, it didn't come back.
§A Whole New World

By the time Noah was 601 years old, on the first day of the first month, the flood on the earth had dried up. Noah opened the cover of the ark and saw dry ground. By the 27th day of the second month, the earth was completely dry.

Then God said to Noah, “Alright, time to get out of the ark—you, your wife, your sons, and their wives. Bring out every living creature with you—the birds, the animals, and all the critters that crawl on the ground. Let them go nuts and have tons of babies and fill the earth.”
So Noah got out, along with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives. All the animals, all the crawling creatures, and all the birds—everything that moves on the earth—left the ark, family by family.
§A Promise from God

Noah built an altar for God and took some of all the clean animals and clean birds and offered them as burnt offerings on the altar. When God smelled the sweet aroma, he thought to himself, “I’m never going to curse the ground again because of humans, even though their hearts are kinda bent toward evil from the time they're young. And I’ll never again destroy every living thing as I’ve just done."
As long as the earth exists, there will always be planting and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night. That will never stop.”

title: God's Rainbow Promise and a Family Mess-Up
paragraphs: § A Fresh Start

God gave Noah and his sons a huge blessing. He was like, "Go out there, have a ton of kids, and fill up the whole planet! Every animal, bird, and fish is gonna be scared of you. You're in charge of them now. You can eat any living creature. Just like I gave you plants, now you can have it all. But, one rule: no eating meat that still has its lifeblood in it. That's a no-go."

"And listen up," God said, "If anyone takes a human life, I'm gonna hold them accountable—whether it's an animal or another person. Whoever kills a person, by a person they will be killed. Why? Because I made humans in my own image, to be like me. So your job is to have lots of kids and fill the Earth with life!"
§ The Rainbow Promise

Then God told Noah and his sons, "I'm making a promise, a covenant, with you, your future kids, and every living thing that was on the ark with you. Here's the deal: I will never again wipe out everything on Earth with a flood. A worldwide flood? Never happening again."

"And to prove it," God said, "I'm putting a rainbow in the clouds. It's a sign of my promise between me and the Earth. From now on, whenever I bring clouds and a rainbow shows up, I'll remember my promise. I'll see it and remember this forever-covenant between me and every living thing on the planet." God finished by saying, "This rainbow is the official sign of the promise I've made with everything on Earth."
§ A Drunken Mistake
The sons who got off the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan. The whole world's population came from these three guys and their families.
Noah, who was a farmer, planted the first-ever vineyard. One day, he drank some of the wine he made, got totally drunk, and passed out naked inside his tent.

Ham, Canaan's dad, saw his father naked. Instead of helping, he went and told his two brothers who were outside. Shem and Japheth grabbed a blanket, walked in backward without looking, and covered their dad up. They made sure not to see him naked.

When Noah woke up from his hangover, he found out what his youngest son, Ham, had done. He was furious and said, "Cursed be Canaan! He will be the lowest of slaves to his brothers. Blessed be God, the God of Shem, but Canaan will be his slave. May God give Japheth tons of space, and may he live with Shem. But Canaan will be their slave."
§ The End of an Era
Noah lived for 350 more years after the flood. In total, he lived 950 years. And then he died.

title: Noah's Kids and Their Family Trees
paragraphs: § Noah's Family Tree
Alright, so here's the rundown of Noah's sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. After the big flood, they started having their own kids.

Japheth's sons were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras. Gomer's sons were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah. Javan's sons were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim. All the people who lived by the sea came from these guys, each group in their own spot, with their own families and languages.
§ Ham's Line
Ham's sons were Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan. Cush's sons were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah's sons were Sheba and Dedan.

Cush also had a son named Nimrod. This dude was the first absolute legend warrior on the planet. He was an insane hunter, so good that people would say, "You're a beast hunter, just like Nimrod!" His kingdom started with Babel, and then he took over Erech, Akkad, and Calneh in Shinar. From there, he went up to Asshur and built the cities of Nineveh, Rehoboth Ir, Calah, and Resen, which was between Nineveh and the mega-city Calah.
Egypt was the ancestor of the Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim, Pathrusim, Casluhim (where the Philistines came from), and the Kaphtorim.

Canaan’s first son was Sidon, and then he had Heth. From him came the Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites. Later on, the Canaanite people spread out from Sidon all the way down to Gerar and Gaza, and then east to Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Lasha.
So yeah, that's the whole family line of Ham, sorted by family, language, country, and nation.
§ Shem's Line
Shem, who was Japheth's older brother, had kids too. He was the ancestor of all of Eber's descendants.
Shem's sons were Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram. Aram's sons were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
Arphaxad had Shelah, and Shelah had Eber. Eber had two sons. The first was named Peleg, which means 'division', because during his time, everyone on Earth got split up. His other son was Joktan.

Joktan had a bunch of sons: Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. Their territory stretched from Mesha all the way to the eastern mountains of Sephar.
So that's the family line of Shem, all sorted by family, language, country, and nation.
This is the complete family tree of Noah's sons, and how they grew into different nations. From these guys, nations spread out all over the world after the flood.

title: God Mixes Up Languages at Babel Tower
paragraphs: Back in the day, everyone on Earth spoke the same language. As people moved eastward, they found a nice plain in Shinar and decided to settle there. They were like, "Yo, let's make some bricks and bake 'em real good." They used these bricks instead of stone and tar for their glue.
Then they got this big idea: "Let's build a massive city with a tower that scrapes the sky! We'll make a name for ourselves, so we don't get scattered all over the place."

So God came down to check out the city and the tower they were building. He saw what was up and said, "Look at this. One group of people, one language. This is just the beginning. Who knows what they'll try next? They'll think they can do anything. Nah, I'm going down there to mix up their language so they can't understand each other."

And just like that, God scattered them all over the world, and they had to stop building the city. That's why it's called Babel, because God turned their language into a bunch of babble. From there, he spread them out across the globe.
§ Shem's Family Line

Here's the deal with Shem's family. When Shem was 100 years old, he had a son named Arphaxad. This was two years after the great flood. After Arphaxad was born, Shem lived for another 500 years and had more kids.
When Arphaxad was 35, he had Shelah. Then he lived for another 403 years and had more kids.
When Shelah was 30, he had Eber. Then he lived for another 403 years and had more kids.
When Eber was 34, he had Peleg. Then he lived for another 430 years and had more kids.
When Peleg was 30, he had Reu. Then he lived for another 209 years and had more kids.
When Reu was 32, he had Serug. Then he lived for another 207 years and had more kids.
When Serug was 30, he had Nahor. Then he lived for another 200 years and had more kids.
When Nahor was 29, he had Terah. Then he lived for another 119 years and had more kids.
When Terah was 70, he had Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
§ Terah's Family
So here's Terah's story. He was the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran had a son named Lot. Haran actually died in his hometown, Ur of the Chaldees, before his own dad, Terah, passed away.
Abram and Nahor both got married. Abram's wife was Sarai, and Nahor's wife was Milcah. Milcah was the daughter of his brother Haran, who also had another daughter named Iscah.
Here's the sad part: Sarai couldn't have kids. She was barren.

One day, Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot (Haran's son), and his daughter-in-law Sarai (Abram's wife) and they all left Ur of the Chaldees to go to the land of Canaan. But when they reached a place called Haran, they decided to just stay there.
Terah lived to be 205 years old and died in Haran.

title: Abram's Big Move and a Big Lie
paragraphs: § God's Epic Promise

God told Abram, "Yo, you gotta leave your country, your fam, and your dad's place for a land that I'm gonna show you. I'm gonna make you into a huge nation and bless you big time. I'll make you famous, and you'll be a major blessing to everyone. I'll have your back—anyone who blesses you, I'll bless them. Anyone who messes with you, I'll curse them. Seriously, every family on Earth is gonna be blessed because of you."
§ The Journey Begins

So Abram just did what God said. He bounced, and his nephew Lot went with him. Get this—Abram was 75 years old when he left Haran. He took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all their stuff, and all the people they had gathered in Haran, and they headed out for Canaan. And they made it, no problem. Abram traveled through the land all the way to a place called Shechem, by the big tree of Moreh. Back then, the Canaanites were living in that area.

Then God showed up to Abram and said, "I'm going to give this land to your descendants." So Abram built an altar right there where God had appeared to him. After that, he moved on to the hill country east of Bethel and set up his camp. He built another altar there and prayed to God. Abram just kept on moving, heading south toward the Negev desert.
§ A Risky Plan in Egypt

Then, a huge famine hit the land. It was so bad that Abram had to go down to Egypt to find food. As they were getting close to Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, "Look, let's be real, you're crazy beautiful. When the Egyptians see you, they're gonna be like, 'Whoa, that's his wife!' and they'll totally kill me to get to you. But they'll let you live. So do me a solid: just tell them you're my sister. That way, they'll be cool with me and I won't get killed because of you."

When Abram got to Egypt, the Egyptians took one look at his wife and were like, "OMG, she's absolutely stunning." The Pharaoh's officials were raving about her to him, and next thing you know, she was taken to live in Pharaoh's palace.

Because of her, Abram was treated like an honored guest. He got loaded with sheep, cattle, donkeys, servants, and camels. But then God started hitting Pharaoh and his whole palace with some serious plagues, all because of Sarai, Abram's wife.

Pharaoh called Abram and was like, "Dude, what have you done to me?! Why didn't you just tell me she was your wife? Why'd you say, 'She's my sister,' so I ended up taking her as my wife? Here, take your wife back—and get out!" Pharaoh then ordered his men to escort Abram, his wife, and all his stuff out of the country.

title: Abram and Lot Split: God's Epic Promise
paragraphs: § Back in the Mix

So Abram bounced from Egypt and headed back to the Negev. He had his wife, all his stuff, and Lot was still tagging along. By this point, Abram was seriously rich—like, loaded with cattle, silver, and gold. He kept moving from the Negev, setting up camp along the way, until he got back to Bethel. That was the spot where he first pitched his tent between Bethel and Ai and built his first altar. Abram took some time there to pray to God.
§ Family Drama

Lot, who was rolling with Abram, was also super rich with his own sheep, cattle, and tents. The problem was, the land couldn't handle both of them. They had way too much stuff and there just wasn't enough space. This led to some major drama, with fights breaking out between Abram's and Lot's shepherds. On top of that, the Canaanites and Perizzites were already living there, so things were crowded.

Abram told Lot, "Look, we can't be fighting. Our shepherds shouldn't be fighting either. We're family, man. Let's just split up. The whole land is right here. If you go left, I'll go right. If you go right, I'll go left. Simple."
§ The Big Split

Lot took a good look around and saw the entire Jordan plain. It was super green and well-watered, kind of like God's own garden or even like Egypt (this was before God wrecked Sodom and Gomorrah). It stretched all the way to Zoar. So, Lot was like, "I'll take that!" and he claimed the whole Jordan plain for himself, heading east.

And that's how the uncle and nephew went their separate ways. Abram stayed in Canaan, while Lot set up his camp in the cities of the plain, getting pretty close to Sodom. Just so you know, the people of Sodom were seriously bad news—like, openly sinning against God.
§ God's Epic Promise

After Lot took off, God said to Abram, "Open your eyes and look around. North, south, east, west—everything you see, this whole land, I'm giving it to you and your kids forever. I'm going to make your family so huge, you won't even be able to count them. It'll be like trying to count all the dust on the Earth. So get up and start walking. Check out the whole country, because I'm giving it all to you."
So Abram packed up his tent and moved. He went and settled by the great trees of Mamre in Hebron, and right there, he built another altar to God.

title: Abram's Epic Rescue Mission
paragraphs: § The Great King War

So check it, four kings—Amraphel from Shinar, Arioch from Ellasar, Kedorlaomer from Elam, and Tidal from Goiim—decided to roll out and start a war. Their targets? Five other kings: Bera from Sodom, Birsha from Gomorrah, Shinab from Admah, Shemeber from Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (also known as Zoar).

These five kings had been totally owned by Kedorlaomer for twelve years. But in the thirteenth year, they were like, "Nah, we're done," and they rebelled. All these guys met up to fight in the Siddim Valley, which is now the Salt Sea.
§ Kedorlaomer Strikes Back

A year later, Kedorlaomer and his crew came back with a vengeance. They went on a total rampage, crushing the Rephaim, the Zuzim, the Emim, and the Horites. They pushed all the way to the edge of the desert. On their way back, they wrecked the whole area of the Amalekites and the Amorites.

That's when the five-king squad marched out to face them. It was a 4-on-5 battle in the Siddim Valley. But the valley was a mess, full of sticky tar pits. When the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah tried to escape, they fell right into the pits. The rest of their guys scattered and ran for the mountains.

The four kings took everything from Sodom and Gomorrah—all their stuff, all their food, everything. And to make it worse, they also kidnapped Lot, Abram's nephew who was living in Sodom, and took all his possessions too.
§ Abram's Rescue Mission
Someone who escaped the battle ran and told Abram what happened. Abram was chilling by the oaks of Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers, Eshcol and Aner, were Abram's allies.

When Abram heard his nephew was captured, he didn't hesitate. He gathered his 318 trained guys, all born in his household, and went after the enemy, chasing them all the way to Dan. That night, Abram and his squad split up, attacked from different sides, and totally surprised them. They chased the enemy all the way to Hobah, north of Damascus.
They got everything back—all the stolen stuff, Abram's nephew Lot, his belongings, and all the captured people, including the women.
§ A Royal Blessing

After Abram came back from this epic win, the king of Sodom came out to greet him. Then this other king, Melchizedek of Salem, who was a priest of the Most High God, showed up with bread and wine. He blessed Abram, saying:
"May Abram be blessed by the Most High God, the Creator of heaven and earth. And praise to the Most High God, who gave you this victory over your enemies."
It was a huge moment. Abram was so grateful that he gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything he had recovered.
§ Abram Keeps It Real
The king of Sodom then told Abram, "Hey, just give me my people back. You can keep all the loot for yourself."

But Abram was like, "Nah, I'm good. I made a promise to the Most High God, the Creator of heaven and earth, that I wouldn't take a single thing from you, not even a thread or a shoelace. I don't want you ever saying, 'I'm the one who made Abram rich.' My guys already ate, so that's fine. And my allies, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre, they should get their fair share. But for me? I'm not taking anything."

title: God's Epic Promise to Abram
paragraphs: § God's Covenant Promise
After all this went down, God's word came to Abram in a vision, like a super vivid dream. 'Don't be scared, Abram. I've got your back. Your reward is gonna be huge!'

But Abram was like, 'God, my King, what good are your gifts if I don't have any kids? My servant Eliezer from Damascus is gonna get everything.' Abram went on, 'Look, you haven't given me any children, so now some guy who works for me is gonna inherit it all.'
Then God's message came through loud and clear: 'Chill, he's not your heir. A son from your own body will be your heir.'
Then God took him outside and said, 'Look up at the sky. Try to count the stars. Can you even? That's how many descendants you're gonna have! You're going to have a massive family, Abram!'
And Abram actually believed it! He trusted God! And because of that, God said he was 'all good with God.'
§ A Weird Ceremony
God kept going, 'I'm the same God who brought you from Ur of the Chaldees to give you this land to own.'
Abram asked, 'My King, God, how can I be sure it'll all be mine?'
God said, 'Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old goat, a three-year-old ram, a dove, and a young pigeon.'

So Abram brought all the animals, cut them in half, and laid the pieces across from each other. But he didn't cut the birds. Vultures started swooping down to eat the carcasses, but Abram shooed them away. As the sun started to set, Abram fell into a super deep sleep, and then this creepy, dark, and heavy feeling of dread washed over him.
§ A Glimpse of the Future

God told Abram, 'Listen up: your descendants will be foreigners in a land that's not theirs. They'll be slaves and get treated horribly for 400 years. But then I'll bring the hammer down on the nation they serve, and your kids will march out of there with tons of loot. But not you. You'll live a long, full life and die peacefully. It won't be until the fourth generation that your descendants come back here, because the Amorites are still deep in their sin.'

When the sun was totally gone and it was pitch black, a smoking firepot and a blazing torch passed between the animal halves. That's when God made a solid promise with Abram: 'I'm giving this land to your descendants, from the Nile River in Egypt all the way to the Euphrates River in Assyria—the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites, Hittites, Perizzites, Rephaim, Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites.'

title: The OG Surrogate Mom Drama
paragraphs: So, Abram's wife, Sarai, still hadn't had any kids. She had this Egyptian servant girl named Hagar. One day, Sarai tells Abram, 'Look, God's obviously not letting me have a baby. So, go sleep with my servant. Maybe I can start a family through her.' And Abram was like, 'Alright, bet.'

So Sarai, Abram's wife, literally gave her Egyptian servant Hagar to her husband Abram to be like, a second wife. This all went down after Abram had been living in Canaan for ten years. He slept with Hagar, and boom, she got pregnant. The second Hagar found out she was pregnant, she started acting all high and mighty, totally dissing Sarai.

Sarai went straight to Abram and was like, 'This is all your fault! I'm getting treated like dirt here. I give you my servant, and the moment she gets pregnant, she acts like I'm nothing. Let God figure out who's in the right.'
'She's your servant, you handle it,' Abram said. So Sarai started being really harsh to Hagar, and Hagar just ran away.
§Hagar on the Run

An angel of God found her by a spring out in the desert on the road to Shur. The angel asked, 'Hagar, Sarai's servant, what are you doing out here?' She answered, 'I'm running away from my boss, Sarai.'

The angel of God told her, 'Go back to your boss and just deal with her. And listen, I'm going to give you so many descendants, you won't even be able to count them all. You're going to have a son, and you need to name him Ishmael, because God heard you when you were in trouble. He's gonna be a total wild card, a real fighter, always getting into it with people. He'll be stirring up drama with his own family all the time.'
She gave a name to the God who spoke to her: 'You are the God who sees me.' She was like, 'OMG, for real? I just saw the one who sees me!'
That's legit how the spring got its name: Beer-lahai-roi, which means 'The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.' It's still there, between Kadesh and Bered.
So, Hagar had Abram's son, and Abram named him Ishmael. Abram was 86 years old when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael.

title: God's Covenant Promise with Abraham
paragraphs: § A New Name and a Big Promise
When Abram was 99, God just showed up and was like, “Yo, I’m the Almighty God. Live your life all out for me. I’m making a serious promise between us, and I’m gonna give you a massive family.”

Abram was so shook, he just fell on his face. Then God said, “This is my deal with you: you’re gonna be the father of a ton of nations. Your name isn’t Abram anymore, it’s Abraham. It means ‘father of many nations.’ For real, I’m gonna make you the father of fathers. Nations will come from you, and kings will be your descendants. This promise is between me and you, and it’s for your kids and their kids, forever and ever. I’m your God, and I’ll be their God too. And I’m giving you and your descendants this land you’re just chilling in now, the whole land of Canaan, to own forever. And I’ll be their God.”
§ The Sign of the Promise

God kept talking to Abraham, “And you? You gotta respect my promise, you and all your descendants, for all time. This is the promise you have to keep, and it includes all your descendants: every single guy needs to be circumcised. You’ll do this by cutting off the foreskin, and that’ll be the sign of our deal. Every baby boy will be circumcised when he’s eight days old, forever and ever. This goes for slaves born in your house and even slaves you bought from other places who aren’t related to you. Make sure you circumcise your own kids and anyone you bring in. That way, my promise will be literally cut into your body, a permanent mark of my permanent promise. Any guy who isn’t circumcised will be cut off from his people—he broke my promise.”
§ Sarah's New Name and a Surprise Baby

God wasn’t done yet. He said to Abraham, “And your wife, Sarai? Don’t call her Sarai anymore. Call her Sarah. I’m gonna bless her, for real! I’m giving you a son through her! Oh man, I’m gonna bless her so much. Nations will come from her, and kings of nations will come from her.”
Abraham fell on his face again. But this time, he laughed. He was thinking, “For real? A 100-year-old dude is gonna be a dad? And Sarah, at 90, is gonna have a baby?”
He pulled himself together and said to God, “Yo, just please keep Ishmael safe and sound!”

But God was like, “That’s not what I’m talking about. Your wife, Sarah, is gonna have a baby boy. You’re gonna name him Isaac, which means ‘Laughter.’ I’m gonna make my forever promise with him and his descendants.

“And about Ishmael? Yeah, I heard you. I’ll bless him too. He’ll have a ton of kids, a huge family. He’ll be the father of twelve princes, and I’ll make him a great nation. But my main promise, my covenant, is with Isaac, who Sarah will have about this time next year.”
Then God finished talking with Abraham and left.
§ Keeping the Promise

That very same day, Abraham took his son Ishmael and all his servants, everyone from his household, and circumcised them, just like God told him to. Abraham was 99 when he was circumcised, and his son Ishmael was 13. Abraham and Ishmael got circumcised on the same day, along with all the servants in his house, no matter where they came from. Everyone got circumcised with him.

title: God's Surprise Visit and an Epic Bargain
paragraphs: § A Surprise Visit

So, God showed up at Abraham's place by the big oak trees of Mamre. Abraham was just chilling at his tent's entrance, trying to escape the crazy heat of the day. He looked up and, boom, three guys were standing right there. He bolted from his tent to say what's up and bowed down to them.

He was like, "Yo, Master, if you're cool with it, please hang out with me for a bit. I'll get some water so you can wash your feet. Just chill under this tree. I'll grab some food to get you energized for your trip, since you're passing by my spot anyway."
They were like, "For sure. Go for it."
Abraham rushed into the tent to find Sarah and said, "Quick! Grab three cups of our best flour, knead it, and make some bread."

Then Abraham sprinted to the cattle pen, picked out a super plump calf, and handed it to his servant who got it ready, like, instantly. He then grabbed some cheese curds and milk, and brought them out with the roasted calf. He set the whole meal in front of the guys and just stood there under the tree while they ate.
§ A Mind-Blowing Promise
The men asked him, "So, where's your wife, Sarah?"
He said, "She's in the tent."
One of them said, "I'm gonna come back around this time next year. And when I do, your wife Sarah will have a son." Sarah was totally eavesdropping from the tent opening, right behind the guy.

Now, Abraham and Sarah were super old by this point, like, ancient. Sarah was way past the age of having babies. So, Sarah just laughed to herself, thinking, "Seriously? An old lady like me? Get pregnant? With this old dude as my husband?"

Then God said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh and say, 'Me? Have a baby? An old woman like me?' Is anything, like, actually too hard for God? I'll be back around this time next year, and Sarah will have a baby."
Sarah totally lied. She said, "I didn't laugh," 'cause she was scared.
But he was like, "Yeah, you did. You laughed."
§ Abraham's Epic Bargain
When the men got up to leave, they headed towards Sodom. Abraham walked with them to see them off.

Then God thought, "Should I really hide what I'm about to do from Abraham? Abraham's gonna become this huge, strong nation, and all the nations on Earth are gonna be blessed because of him. Yeah, I've chosen him to teach his kids and future family to live God's way—to be kind, generous, and fair. That way, I can do for Abraham everything I promised him."

God went on, "The cries from Sodom and Gomorrah are getting crazy loud; the sin in those cities is off the charts. I'm going down there to see for myself if it's as bad as everyone's saying. Then I'll know for sure."
The men took off for Sodom, but Abraham stood right in God's way, blocking him.

Abraham was like, "Are you for real? Are you really gonna wipe out the good people with the bad? What if there are, like, fifty good people left in the city? Are you just gonna lump them all together and destroy everything? Wouldn't you spare the city for those fifty innocent people? I can't even believe you'd do that, killing the good and the bad like they're the same. Doesn't the Judge of the whole Earth have to be fair?"
God said, "If I find fifty good people in the city of Sodom, I'll spare the whole place just for them."

Abraham came back with, "Look, I know I'm just a guy made of dust, but can I say one more thing to my Master? What if there are only forty-five good people, not fifty? Would you destroy the city just because of five missing people?"
He said, "I won't destroy it if there are forty-five."
Abraham tried again, "What if you only find forty?"
"I won't destroy it for forty either."
He said, "Master, please don't get mad at me, but what if only thirty are found?"
"Nope, I won't do it if I find thirty."
He kept going, "I know I'm really testing your patience, Master, but what about for twenty?"
"I won't destroy it for twenty."
He just wouldn't give up. "Don't get angry, Master—this is the last time, I swear. What if you only find ten?"
"For the sake of just ten, I won't destroy the city."
When God finished talking with Abraham, he left. And Abraham went home.

title: Sodom's Downfall and a Shocking Family Secret
paragraphs: § An Awkward Welcome

That evening, the two angels showed up in Sodom. Lot was chilling by the city gate and when he saw them, he got up, bowed down, and was like, “Hey guys, please come crash at my place for the night. You can wash up and then get an early start tomorrow, all refreshed.”
They were like, “Nah, we’re good, we’ll just sleep on the street.”
But Lot was super insistent and wouldn’t take no for an answer. So, they finally gave in and went home with him. Lot cooked them a hot meal, and they all ate.
§ A Vicious Mob

Before they could even go to bed, a huge mob of guys from all over Sodom, young and old, surrounded the house. They were yelling at Lot, “Where are the dudes who are staying with you tonight? Bring them out so we can have sex with them!”

Lot went outside, shutting the door behind him, and pleaded, “Guys, please, don’t be so messed up. Look, I’ve got two daughters who are virgins. I’ll bring them out and you can do whatever you want with them, but please don’t touch these men. They’re my guests.”

But they just yelled back, “Get out of our way! You just show up here and now you think you can tell us what to do? We’ll do way worse to you than to them!” They rushed at Lot and tried to break down the door.

But the two visitors reached out, pulled Lot back inside, and locked the door. Then they zapped the entire mob with blindness, so everyone from the leaders to the followers was just stumbling around in the dark, totally clueless.
§ Time to Bail

The two men said to Lot, “You got any other family here? Sons, daughters, anyone at all in this city? You need to get them out of here, like, right now. We’re about to destroy this place. The cries of the victims have reached God, and He sent us to totally wipe this city off the map.”
So Lot went out and warned his daughters’ fiancés, “You guys have to get out of here! God is about to destroy this city!” But they just laughed and thought he was joking.

As soon as the sun started to rise, the angels were pushing Lot to get a move on. “Hurry up! Get your wife and your two daughters out of here before it’s too late and you get caught up in the city’s punishment.”

But Lot was dragging his feet. So the men, because God was being super merciful, grabbed Lot, his wife, and his daughters by the arm and dragged them to safety outside the city. Once they were out, one of them said, “Now run for your life! Don’t look back, and don’t stop anywhere on the plain. Run to the hills, or you’ll be toast.”
§ A Small Request

But Lot was like, “No way, masters, you can’t be serious! I know you guys have been cool to me and saved my life, which is a huge deal, but I can’t make it to the mountains. Something terrible will probably happen to me there and I’ll die. But look, that town over there is super close. It’s just a tiny place, barely anything. Let me escape there and live. It’s basically just a wide spot in the road.”

“Alright, fine,” he said. “If you insist. I’ll do what you want. I won’t destroy the town you pointed out. But seriously, hurry up. Run! I can’t do anything until you get there.” And that’s why the town was called Zoar, which means “Smalltown.”
§ Total Destruction
The sun was already high in the sky when Lot finally got to Zoar.

Then God made it rain fire and brimstone on Sodom and Gomorrah. It was like a river of lava pouring down from the sky! He destroyed the cities, the whole plain, every single person living there, and everything that grew in the ground.
But Lot’s wife looked back, and she instantly turned into a pillar of salt.

Abraham got up early the next morning and went to the spot where he had stood with God. He looked out over Sodom and Gomorrah and the whole plain, and all he saw was a massive cloud of smoke rising from the earth, like smoke from a giant furnace.
So that’s the story. When God destroyed the cities on the plain, he remembered his boy Abraham and made sure to get Lot out of there before he completely obliterated those cities.
§ A Desperate Plan
Lot was too scared to stay in Zoar, so he left and went to live in the mountains with his two daughters. They ended up living in a cave.

One day, the older daughter said to the younger one, “Dad’s getting old, and there are literally no men left in this whole area for us to have kids with. Let’s get Dad drunk and then sleep with him. It’s the only way we can have kids and keep our family line going.”

So that night, they got their father drunk. The older daughter went in and slept with him, and he was so out of it he had no idea what happened. The next morning, the older sister told the younger one, “Okay, I slept with Dad last night. Tonight, it’s your turn. We’ll get him drunk again, and you go sleep with him. That way, we’ll both have a kid through our dad and our family won’t die out.”
So they got their father drunk again that night, and the younger daughter went in and slept with him. And again, he was totally oblivious and didn’t know a thing.

Both of Lot’s daughters ended up getting pregnant by their own father. The older daughter had a son and named him Moab, and he’s the ancestor of the Moabites today. The younger daughter also had a son and named him Ben-Ammi, and he’s the ancestor of the Ammonites.

title: Abraham's Epic Lie and a King's Close Call
paragraphs: § The "She's My Sister" Rerun

So Abraham moved south to the Negev region and was chilling between Kadesh and Shur. While he was staying in Gerar, he told everyone that his wife, Sarah, was actually his sister. Like, again. So, the king of Gerar, a guy named Abimelech, heard this and sent for Sarah to be part of his crew.
§ God's Dream Intervention

But that night, God showed up in Abimelech's dream and was like, "Yo, you're basically a dead man. That woman you just took? She's married." Abimelech, who hadn't even laid a finger on her, was shook. He pleaded, "Lord, are you going to take out an innocent guy? He's the one who told me, 'She's my sister,' and she even said, 'He's my brother.' I swear, my intentions were totally pure. I had no clue I was doing anything wrong." God replied in the dream, "Yeah, I know you meant well. That's actually why I stopped you from sinning against me and kept you from sleeping with her. Now, you need to give her back to her husband. He's a prophet, and he'll pray for you so you can live. But if you don't return her, I'm telling you, you and your entire household are toast. For real."
§ The Morning After

Abimelech shot out of bed first thing in the morning, gathered all his officials, and told them everything that happened. They were all freaking out. Then Abimelech called Abraham in and was like, "Dude, what have you done to us?! What did I ever do to you that you'd bring this much trouble on me and my kingdom? This is not cool. What you did was seriously messed up." He kept grilling him, "What were you even thinking, pulling a stunt like that?"
§ Abraham's Excuse

Abraham finally explained, "Look, I just figured there was no respect for God in this place and that you guys would kill me to get my wife. Plus, she actually is my half-sister. We have the same dad, just not the same mom. And when God sent me on this whole journey away from my family, I told her, 'Hey, do me a solid. Everywhere we go, just tell people you're my sister.'"
§ Making Things Right

Then Abimelech gave Sarah back to Abraham. On top of that, he threw in a bunch of sheep, cattle, and servants as a gift. He told Abraham, "My whole land is open to you. Feel free to live wherever you want." And he said to Sarah, "Check it out, I gave your 'brother' a thousand pieces of silver. This should prove to everyone that you're totally innocent and clear your name completely. You're good."

Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech. His wife and female servants were able to have kids again. See, God had made it so none of the women in Abimelech's house could get pregnant because of what happened with Abraham's wife, Sarah.

title: A Promise Kept, A Family Divided
paragraphs: § The Promised Son

God showed up for Sarah, just like he promised. And just like he said, Sarah got pregnant and had a son for Abraham in his old age. It happened at the exact time God had scheduled. Abraham named him Isaac, which means "laughter." When Isaac was eight days old, Abraham had him circumcised, following God's instructions. Abraham was 100 years old when Isaac was born.

Sarah was so happy, she said, "God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me! Who would've ever guessed that I'd be nursing a baby at my age? But here I am, I've given my old husband a son!"
The baby grew up and it was time to stop breastfeeding. Abraham threw a huge party to celebrate.
§ Hagar and Ishmael Sent Away

But one day, Sarah saw Hagar's son, Ishmael, making fun of her son, Isaac. She got super mad and told Abraham, "You need to get rid of that slave woman and her son. Her son is not going to get any of my son's inheritance!"

This was really tough for Abraham to hear. After all, Ishmael was his son too. But God told him, "Don't worry about the boy or Hagar. Just do what Sarah says. Your family line will continue through Isaac. And don't worry about Ishmael, I'll make a great nation out of him too, because he's your son."

So, the next morning, Abraham got up early, packed some food and water for Hagar, and sent her and the boy away. She wandered into the Beersheba desert. When the water ran out, she put the boy under a bush and walked about 50 yards away. She couldn't bear to watch him die, so she just sat there and cried her eyes out.

But God heard the boy crying. An angel called down from heaven, "What's wrong, Hagar? Don't be scared. God heard the boy and knows he's in a tough spot. Get up, go get your son, and hold him tight. I'm going to make him into a great nation."
Just then, God opened her eyes and she saw a well full of water. She ran to it, filled up her canteen, and gave the boy a long, cool drink.
God was with Ishmael as he grew up. He lived in the desert and became a pro archer. He settled in the Paran wilderness, and his mom found him a wife from Egypt.
§ A Treaty at Beersheba

Around that same time, a king named Abimelech and his army commander, Phicol, came to Abraham and said, "Dude, it's obvious that God is with you in everything you do. So, promise me that you won't ever try to trick me or my family. As long as you're living in my land, you have to treat me and my people as well as I've treated you."
Abraham replied, "You got it. I swear."
But then Abraham brought up an issue. "Your servants stole a well from me," he told Abimelech.
Abimelech was like, "I had no idea who did that. You never said anything to me about it. This is the first I'm hearing of it."
So, they made a deal. Abraham gave Abimelech some sheep and cattle. Then, Abraham set aside seven more sheep.
Abimelech asked, "What's with the seven extra sheep?"
Abraham explained, "When you accept these seven sheep, it's proof that I'm the one who dug this well, and that it belongs to me."

That's why they named the place Beersheba, which means "Oath-Well," because they both made a promise there. After they made their deal, Abimelech and his commander Phicol went back to their own territory.
Abraham planted a special tree in Beersheba and prayed to God, the Eternal God. And Abraham lived in that Philistine area for a long, long time.

title: A Test of Faith: Abraham and Isaac
paragraphs: § The Ultimate Test
So after all this went down, God decided to test Abraham’s loyalty. He called out, “Abraham!” and Abraham replied, “Yeah? What’s up?”
God said, “Take your son, your only son Isaac, the one you love so much, and go to the region of Moriah. There, you’re to sacrifice him as a burnt offering on one of the mountains I’ll show you.”

Abraham, being the dedicated guy he was, got up super early the next morning. He saddled his donkey, and took two of his servants and his son Isaac with him. He had already chopped the wood for the offering, and they set off for the place God told him about. On the third day, Abraham looked up and saw the spot from a distance. He told his servants, “Yo, just wait here with the donkey. The boy and I are going over there to worship, and we’ll be right back.”
§ A Father and Son's Journey
Abraham handed the wood for the burnt offering to Isaac to carry, while he carried the flint and the knife. As they were walking, Isaac turned to his dad and said, “Hey, Dad?”
“Yeah, son?”
“So, we’ve got the flint and the wood… but where’s the lamb for the offering?”
Abraham answered, “Don’t worry, son. God will provide the lamb.” And they continued their journey together.
§ The Altar

When they got to the place God had directed them to, Abraham built an altar and arranged the wood on it. Then, he tied up his son Isaac and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood. He reached for the knife, about to sacrifice his son.
But just then, an angel of God called out to him from heaven, “Abraham! Abraham!”
“I’m here!” he answered.
“Don’t you dare lay a hand on that boy!” the angel said. “Don’t hurt him in any way. Now I know that you truly fear God, because you were willing to sacrifice your own son, your only son, for me.”

Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. He went and got the ram, and sacrificed it as a burnt offering instead of his son. Abraham named that place “Yahweh-Yireh,” which means “The Lord Will Provide.” And to this day, people say, “On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.”
§ A Promise Reconfirmed

The angel of God called out to Abraham from heaven a second time, saying, “I swear by myself, declares the Lord, that because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son, I will surely bless you and make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will take possession of the cities of their enemies, and through your offspring all nations on earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed me.”
Then Abraham returned to his servants, and they all went back to Beersheba, where Abraham settled down.
§ Family Update

After all this, Abraham got some news about his brother Nahor. Turns out, his wife Milcah had given him a bunch of kids: Uz the firstborn, his brother Buz, Kemuel (the father of Aram), Kesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel. And Bethuel was the father of Rebekah. These were the eight sons Milcah had with Nahor, Abraham’s brother. Nahor also had four other children with his concubine, Reumah: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

title: Abraham Buys a Forever Home for Sarah
paragraphs: § A Place to Bury Sarah
Sarah lived to be 127 years old. She died in a place called Kiriath Arba (which is now Hebron) in the land of Canaan. Abraham was obviously heartbroken and cried a lot.

After a while, Abraham got up and went to talk to the local Hittites. He was like, "Yo, I know I'm just a foreigner here, but could you sell me a piece of land for a burial plot? I need to give my wife a proper burial."

The Hittites were super cool about it and said, "Dude, you're not just some random outsider. You're like a prince of God to us! You can bury your wife in the best burial spot we have. Seriously, nobody here would say no to you."
§ Buying the Field

Abraham was really grateful and bowed to them. He said, "If you guys are for real about helping me, could you do me a solid and talk to Ephron, Zohar's son? Ask him to sell me the cave of Machpelah at the end of his field. I'll pay full price for it, right here in front of you all as witnesses."

Ephron, who was one of the Hittite leaders, spoke up in front of everyone, "No way, my dude! I can't do that. But look, the field is yours. It's a gift. I'm giving you the field and the cave. Everyone here is a witness. Go ahead and bury your wife."
Abraham bowed again to everyone and said to Ephron, "Please, let me pay for it. Just take the money so I can bury my wife."
Ephron replied, "Look, if you're gonna insist... what's 400 silver coins between friends? Just go and bury your wife."
So, Abraham agreed and paid Ephron the 400 silver shekels, using the standard rate everyone agreed on.

And that's the story of how Ephron's field near Mamre—the field, the cave, and all the trees—officially became Abraham's property. The Hittite council witnessed the whole deal. Then Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave on that field. The land and the cave were officially transferred from the Hittites to Abraham as his own burial plot.

title: Finding Isaac's Perfect Match
paragraphs: § A Mission for Isaac's Future Wife

Abraham was super old by now, and God had seriously blessed him in every single way. He called over his most trusted servant, the guy in charge of everything, and said, “Put your hand under my thigh and make a promise to God, the God of heaven and earth. You have to swear you won’t get a wife for my son Isaac from any of the local Canaanite girls. Instead, you’ve got to go back to my homeland, to my relatives, and find a wife for him there.”
The servant was like, “But what if the girl isn’t willing to leave her home and come all the way back with me? Should I take your son Isaac back to your old country then?”

“No way!” Abraham shot back. “Absolutely not. Don’t you dare take my son back there. The God of heaven, who brought me from my father’s house and my homeland, promised me, ‘I’m giving this land to your descendants.’ He’ll send his angel ahead of you to make sure you get a wife for my son from there. If the woman refuses to come, then you’re free from this promise. But whatever you do, don’t take my son back.” So the servant put his hand under his master Abraham’s thigh and made the solemn promise.
§ The Test at the Well

The servant took ten of his master’s camels, packed a bunch of amazing gifts from his master, and set off for Aram Naharaim, to the city of Nahor. When he got there, he had the camels kneel down by a well outside the city. It was evening, the time when women usually came out to get water. Then he prayed, “O God, the God of my master Abraham, please give me success today. Be kind to my master Abraham. Look, I’m standing here by the spring, and the young women of the town are coming to get water. Here’s the sign: I’ll say to a girl, ‘Please, let me have a drink from your jug.’ If she answers, ‘Sure, drink up, and I’ll water your camels, too’—let her be the one you have chosen for your servant Isaac. That’s how I’ll know you’re showing your faithful love to my master.”
§ God's Answer Arrives

He had barely finished praying when, believe it or not, Rebekah showed up. She was the daughter of Bethuel, who was the son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor. She was carrying a water jug on her shoulder. The girl was seriously beautiful, a total knockout, and a virgin. She went down to the spring, filled her jug, and started walking back up. The servant ran to meet her and said, “Please, could I have a little sip of water from your jug?”

“Of course, sir, drink,” she said. She quickly lowered the jug and held it for him to drink. After he finished, she said, “I’ll get water for your camels, too, until they’ve had all they want.” She quickly emptied her jug into the trough for the animals, ran back to the well to get more water, and kept going until all the camels were watered. The man just watched her, totally silent, wondering if this was for real. Was this God’s answer? Was his trip a success or not?
§ Gifts and Questions

When the camels were done drinking, the man pulled out some expensive gifts: a gold nose ring and two heavy gold bracelets. He gave them to her and asked, “Tell me, whose daughter are you? And do you think your father has a guest room where we could spend the night?”
She answered, “I’m the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor and Milcah. And yeah, we totally have room for you to stay. We’ve got plenty of straw and feed for the camels, too.”
The man bowed his head and worshiped God, saying, “Praise be to God, the God of my master Abraham. You have been so kind and faithful to my master. You led me straight to my master’s relatives!”
The girl then ran off and told her mom’s whole household everything that had just happened.
§ A Warm Welcome

Now, Rebekah had a brother named Laban. As soon as he saw the nose ring and the bracelets on his sister’s arms and heard her story about what the man said, Laban ran outside to the well. The man was still standing there with his camels. Laban went up to him and said, “Come on in, you who are blessed by God! Why are you just standing out here? I’ve already got the house ready for you and a place for your camels.”

So the man went into the house. They unloaded the camels and gave them straw and feed. Then they brought water so the man and his crew could wash their feet. When they brought out food, the servant said, “I’m not eating until I’ve told you why I’m here.”
“Okay,” Laban said. “Go ahead, tell us.”
§ The Servant's Story

The servant began, “I am Abraham’s servant. God has blessed my master like crazy, and he’s become a great man. God has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male and female servants, camels and donkeys. Then, to top it all off, my master’s wife, Sarah, had a son in her old age, and my master has given him everything he owns. My master made me swear an oath, saying, ‘Don’t get a wife for my son from the Canaanite girls who live here. You must go to my father’s family, to my own relatives, and get a wife for my son there.’

I asked my master, ‘But what if the woman won’t come with me?’ He answered, ‘The God I have always followed will send his angel with you and make your trip successful. You will get a wife for my son from my own family. Then you will be released from your oath. If you go to my family and they refuse to give her to you, you’ll be released from the oath then, too.’

So when I got to the well today, I prayed, ‘God of my master Abraham, if you are willing, please make my mission a success. I’m standing by this well. When a young woman comes to get water, I’ll say, “Please give me a little water from your jug.” If she says, “Sure, and I’ll water your camels too,” let her be the wife you have chosen for my master’s son.’

I had barely finished praying in my head when Rebekah came out with her jug on her shoulder. She went down to the well and drew water, and I said to her, ‘Please, give me a drink.’ She immediately lowered her jug and said, ‘Drink, and I’ll water your camels too.’ So I drank, and she watered the camels. Then I asked her, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She said, ‘The daughter of Bethuel, son of Nahor and Milcah.’ So I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms. Then I bowed down and worshiped God. I praised the God of my master Abraham, who had led me on the right path to find the daughter of my master’s relative for his son.
So now, tell me. Are you going to be kind and faithful to my master? If yes, tell me. If not, tell me that too, so I know what to do next.”
§ The Family Agrees
Laban and Bethuel answered, “This is clearly from God. We can’t say a thing, yes or no. Look, here’s Rebekah. Take her and go. Let her become the wife of your master’s son, just as God has said.”

When Abraham’s servant heard their answer, he bowed down to the ground and worshiped God. Then he brought out gifts of silver and gold, and some beautiful clothes, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and her mother. Then he and his men ate and drank and stayed the night.
§ Time to Go
When they got up the next morning, he said, “Send me back to my master.”
But her brother and mother said, “Let the girl stay with us for about ten more days. Then she can go.”
But he said, “Don’t make me wait! God has made my journey a success. Let me go, so I can return to my master.”
They said, “Okay, let’s call the girl and ask her what she wants to do.” So they called Rebekah and asked her, “Are you willing to go with this man?”
She said, “Yes, I am.”

So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, with her childhood nurse, along with Abraham’s servant and his men. And they blessed Rebekah, saying: “Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon ten thousands! May your descendants conquer the cities of their enemies!”
Then Rebekah and her maids got on the camels and followed the servant. So the servant took Rebekah and left.
§ Isaac Meets Rebekah

Meanwhile, Isaac had come from Beer Lahai Roi and was living in the Negev desert. One evening, he went out into the field to meditate. He looked up and saw camels approaching. Rebekah also looked up and saw Isaac. She got down from her camel and asked the servant, “Who’s that man in the field walking toward us?”
The servant said, “That is my master.” So she took her veil and covered her face.

The servant told Isaac the whole story of what had happened. Then Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother Sarah’s tent. He married her, and she became his wife, and he loved her. And so Isaac was comforted after the death of his mother.

title: A Birthright Traded for a Bowl of Stew
paragraphs: So, Abraham got married again to a woman named Keturah. They had a bunch of sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan's kids were Sheba and Dedan, and Dedan's descendants were the Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim. Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah—all from Keturah's side of the family.

But here's the deal: Abraham gave literally everything he owned to his son, Isaac. As for the sons he had with his other wives, he gave them some nice gifts while he was still alive, but then sent them packing to the east. He wanted to make sure there was plenty of space between them and his main heir, Isaac.

Abraham lived a super long life, 175 years. Then, he took his last breath and died peacefully. He was really old but had lived a full, happy life. His sons, Isaac and Ishmael, buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field Abraham had bought from the Hittites. He was buried right next to his wife, Sarah. After Abraham passed away, God totally blessed his son Isaac, who was living at a place called Beer Lahai Roi.
§ Ishmael's Crew

Now for Ishmael's family tree. Remember him? He was Abraham's son with Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian maid. Here are Ishmael's sons, in the order they were born: Nebaioth (the oldest), Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. Their towns and camps were all named after them, making twelve princes for twelve tribes.

Ishmael lived to be 137. When he died, he was buried with his family. His descendants settled in the area from Havilah all the way to Shur, which is east of Egypt toward Assyria. The thing is, the Ishmaelites pretty much didn't get along with any of their relatives.
§ The Twin Rivalry Begins
Okay, now for Isaac's family story. Abraham had Isaac, and when Isaac was 40, he married Rebekah. She was the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean and the sister of Laban the Aramean.

Rebekah couldn't have kids, so Isaac prayed super hard to God for her. God answered his prayer, and Rebekah got pregnant. But the babies inside her were fighting and kicking like crazy. She was like, "If this is what pregnancy is like, why am I even alive?" So she went to ask God what was going on.
God told her, "You've got two nations inside you, two peoples who are already rivals in your womb. One will be stronger than the other, and the older son will end up serving the younger one."

When it was time to give birth, it turned out she was having twins, for real. The first one came out all red and covered in hair, like he was wearing a fuzzy blanket. They named him Esau, which means "Hairy." His brother came out right after, grabbing onto Esau's heel, so they named him Jacob, which means "Heel-grabber." Isaac was 60 years old when they were born.
§ A Birthright for a Bowl of Stew

The boys grew up. Esau became a skilled hunter, a total outdoors guy. Jacob was more of a quiet dude who preferred to stay inside. Isaac's favorite was Esau because he loved the wild game Esau brought home, but Rebekah's favorite was Jacob.

One day, Jacob was cooking up some stew when Esau came in from the fields, totally starving. Esau said to Jacob, "Quick, give me some of that red stew! I'm dying of hunger!" (That's actually how he got the nickname Edom, which means "Red.")
But Jacob said, "Okay, but you have to trade me. Give me your rights as the firstborn son."
Esau was like, "Dude, I'm about to starve to death! What good are birthright privileges if I'm dead?"

Jacob insisted, "Swear to me first." So Esau did. He swore an oath and traded away his birthright. Then Jacob gave him some bread and the lentil stew. Esau ate, drank, got up, and left. That's how little he cared about his special rights as the firstborn. It was a total shrug-off.
