title: Isaac's Well Drama and God's Unfailing Promise
paragraphs: § God's Big Promise
So, another huge famine hit the land, just as bad as the one in Abraham's time. Isaac decided to go to Gerar, where Abimelech was the king of the Philistines.

But then God appeared to him and said, “Yo, don’t go down to Egypt. Stay right where I tell you. Just hang out in this land, and I'll be with you and bless you like crazy. I’m giving all this land to you and your kids, keeping the promise I made to your father, Abraham. I’ll make your family as massive as the stars in the sky and give them all these lands. And through your descendants, every nation on Earth will get blessed. You know why? Because Abraham listened to me and followed all my rules, commands, and teachings.”
So, Isaac stayed in Gerar.
§ Isaac's Risky Lie

The local guys started asking him about his wife. He told them, “She’s my sister.” He was too scared to say, “She’s my wife,” because he was thinking, “These dudes might kill me to get Rebekah, she’s seriously beautiful.”

After they had been there for a good while, King Abimelech looked out his window one day and saw Isaac getting a little too cozy with his wife, Rebekah. Busted. Abimelech called Isaac over and said, “Okay, so she IS your wife. Why on earth did you tell us she was your sister?”
Isaac replied, “Because I honestly thought I might get killed by someone who wanted her.”

Abimelech was like, “Dude, what were you thinking? One of the men could have easily slept with your wife, and you would have brought a huge mess down on all of us!” Then Abimelech made a decree to everyone: “Anyone who even lays a hand on this man or his wife will be executed. Period.”
§ Well Drama and Jealous Haters

Isaac planted crops in that land and had an insane harvest. God totally blessed him. The guy got richer and richer every single day until he was legit wealthy. He had tons of flocks, herds, and a whole army of servants. It got to the point where the Philistines were super jealous.
They were so petty that they went and filled up all the wells that his father’s servants had dug back in Abraham's time with dirt, completely clogging them.
Finally, Abimelech told Isaac, “You need to leave. You’ve become way too powerful for us.”

So Isaac left and set up camp in the Gerar valley. He started re-digging the wells that were from his father Abraham’s time, which the Philistines had plugged up after Abraham died. He even gave them the same names his father had originally given them.

One day, while Isaac’s servants were digging, they found a well with fresh spring water. But the shepherds from Gerar started a fight with Isaac’s shepherds, yelling, “This water is ours!” So Isaac named the well Esek, which means “Quarrel,” because they fought over it. Then they dug another well, and people argued over that one too, so he named it Sitnah, meaning “Accusation.”

He moved on from there and dug another well. This time, nobody fought over it, so he named it Rehoboth, which means “Wide-Open Spaces.” He said, “Finally! God has given us room to grow and succeed in this land.”

From there, he went up to Beersheba. That very night, God appeared to him and said, “I am the God of your father, Abraham. Don’t be afraid, because I am with you. I will bless you and make your family huge, all for the sake of my servant Abraham.”
Isaac built an altar there and prayed to God. He set up his tent, and his servants started digging yet another well.
§ Making Peace

Then Abimelech came to visit him from Gerar, bringing his advisor Ahuzzath and Phicol, the commander of his army. Isaac asked them, “Why are you guys here? You obviously hate me; you kicked me out of your country.”

They answered, “Look, we’ve seen that God is totally on your side. We want to make a peace treaty with you, a promise that we’ll stay on good terms. We never bothered you; in fact, we were good to you and let you leave in peace. So, for real, God’s blessing is with you!”
Isaac threw a big feast for them, and they all ate and drank together. They got up early the next morning and made a formal oath to each other. Then Isaac said his goodbyes, and they left as friends.

Later that same day, Isaac’s servants came to him with awesome news about the well they were digging: “We hit water!” Isaac named the well Sheba, which means “Oath.” And that’s why the city is called Beersheba, or “Oath-Well,” to this day.
§ Esau's Bad Decisions
When Esau was forty, he married two Hittite women, Judith and Basemath. They made life a living nightmare for Isaac and Rebekah.

title: The Great Blessing Heist: A Family Drama
paragraphs: § Isaac's Last Wish

When Isaac was super old and basically blind, he called for his oldest son, Esau. "My son?"
"Yeah, Dad?"
"Look, I'm an old man," he said. "I could literally die any day now. So do me a solid: grab your bow and arrows, go hunt something, and cook me up one of those awesome meals you know I love. I wanna eat it and give you my official blessing before I check out."
§ Mom's Sketchy Plan

Rebekah was totally eavesdropping on this whole conversation. As soon as Esau was gone, she went straight to her other son, Jacob. "Okay, so I just heard your dad talking to Esau. He was like, 'Bring me some food so I can give you God's official blessing before I die.'"
"So, listen up," she said. "You're gonna do exactly what I say. Go grab two of the best young goats from the flock. I'll cook them up just how your dad likes it. Then you'll take it to him, he'll eat, and he'll bless you before he dies."
§ The Big Scam

"Uh, Mom?" Jacob said. "There's a tiny problem. My brother Esau is, like, a super hairy dude, and I'm all smooth-skinned. What if Dad touches me? He's gonna know I'm messing with him. I'll get a curse instead of a blessing, for real."
"Don't worry about it," his mom said. "If anyone gets cursed, it'll be me. Just do what I told you. Go get the goats."

So he did. He got the goats, brought them to his mom, and she cooked up a meal that was seriously legit, just the way his dad loved it. Then Rebekah grabbed Esau's best clothes and put them on Jacob. She used the goatskins to cover his hands and the back of his neck. Then she handed him the amazing meal and some fresh bread she'd just baked.

He went to his dad and said, "Dad?"
"Yeah?" he said. "Which son are you?"
Jacob said, "It's me, your firstborn, Esau. I did what you said. So, sit up and eat the food I hunted so you can give me your blessing."
Isaac was like, "Whoa, that was fast. How'd you get it so quickly?"
"Because your God totally hooked me up."
Isaac said, "Come closer, let me feel you. Are you for real my son Esau?"
So Jacob got closer, and Isaac felt him. "Hmm, the voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are Esau's hands." He couldn't tell it was Jacob because his hands were hairy, just like his brother's.
But right before he gave the blessing, he asked one more time, "You're absolutely sure? You are my son Esau?"
"Yep. That's me."
§ The Stolen Blessing

"Okay, bring the food," Isaac said. "I'll eat my son's game and give you my blessing." Jacob brought it, and he ate. He brought him some wine too, and he drank.
Then Isaac said, "Come here and give me a kiss, son."
He got close and kissed him, and Isaac smelled his clothes. Finally, he gave the blessing: "Ahhh. The smell of my son is like a field blessed by God. May God give you plenty of rain and rich soil for tons of grain and wine. May people serve you and nations bow down to you. You will be the boss of your brothers, and your mother's sons will bow to you. Whoever curses you will be cursed, and whoever blesses you will be blessed."
§ The Aftermath

Literally the second after Jacob left with the blessing, Esau showed up from his hunt. He had also cooked an awesome meal. He went to his dad and said, "Dad, get up and eat the food your son hunted, so you can give me your blessing."
His dad, Isaac, said, "Who are you?"
"It's me, your son, your firstborn, Esau."
Isaac started shaking like crazy. "Then who was it that just hunted game and brought it to me? I just finished eating before you got here. And I blessed him—and the blessing is final!"
When Esau heard that, he let out a loud, bitter sob. "Dad! Can't you bless me too?"
"Your brother tricked me," he said. "He came and stole your blessing."
Esau was furious. "No wonder his name is Jacob, the 'Deceiver'! He's tricked me twice now. First, he took my birthright, and now he's taken my blessing!" He begged, "Don't you have any blessing left for me?"
Isaac answered, "Look, I've made him your boss, and all his relatives his servants. I've given him all the grain and wine. There's nothing left for you, my son."
"But you don't have a single blessing left for me, Dad? Please, bless me too!" Esau just broke down and cried.
§ Esau's Rough Future

Isaac said to him, "Well, your life will be far from the good stuff on earth and the rain from the sky. You'll have to live by fighting, always struggling, and you'll have to serve your brother. But when you can't take it anymore, you'll break free."
§ The Revenge Plot

Esau was seething with rage at Jacob because of the blessing. He thought to himself, "The time to mourn my dad's death is coming soon. And right after that, I'm going to kill my brother Jacob."
Someone told Rebekah what Esau was planning, so she called Jacob and said, "Listen, your brother Esau is plotting to get revenge on you. He's going to kill you. So you need to listen to me. Get out of here, now. Run to my brother Laban's place in Haran. Stay with him for a while until your brother chills out, until he's not so angry anymore and forgets what you did. Then I'll send for you. Why would I want to lose both of my sons on the same day?"
Then Rebekah went to Isaac and said, "I am so over these Hittite women. If Jacob marries one of them too, I'll have nothing to live for."

title: Jacob's Ladder Dream and His Epic Vow
paragraphs: So, Isaac called Jacob over, gave him his blessing, and was like, "Yo, do NOT marry a girl from Canaan. Get outta here, like, right now. Go to Paddan Aram, to your grandpa Bethuel's fam. Find a wife there from your Uncle Laban's daughters."

"And for real, may the Almighty God bless you big time, give you tons of kids, so you become a huge crew of people. And may you get the same blessing Abraham got, for you and all your future kids, so you can own this land you're on, the land God promised to Abraham."
So Isaac sent Jacob on his way. He bounced to Paddan Aram, to Laban, who was the son of Bethuel the Aramean and the brother of Rebekah, Jacob and Esau's mom.

Meanwhile, Esau found out that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him off to Paddan Aram to get a wife, telling him straight up, "No Canaanite girls." And Jacob actually listened to his parents and left. When Esau saw how much his dad hated the Canaanite women, he went and married one of Ishmael's daughters, Mahalath, who was Nebaioth's sister. And yeah, this was on top of the wives he already had.
§ Jacob's Dream at Bethel

Jacob dipped from Beersheba and headed to Haran. He found a random spot to crash for the night 'cause the sun was down. He grabbed a rock for a pillow (for real) and went to sleep. And then he had this epic dream: there was a massive ladder set up on the ground, and it went all the way up to the sky. And get this—angels were going up and down on it.

Then, boom, God was right there in front of him, saying, "I'm God, the God of your grandpa Abraham and your dad Isaac. This ground you're sleeping on? I'm giving it to you and your kids. Your family's gonna be like the dust of the earth—they're gonna spread out in every direction. All the people on earth will be blessed because of you and your fam. For real. I'm with you, I'll protect you wherever you go, and I'll bring you back to this exact spot. I'm not leaving your side until I do everything I promised."

Jacob woke up and was like, "Whoa, God is actually in this place, and I had no idea!" He was totally freaked out. He whispered, "This is insane. So cool. So holy. This is God's house. This is the gate to heaven."

First thing in the morning, Jacob got up, took that rock he used as a pillow, and set it up as a memorial. He poured oil on it to make it official. He named the place Bethel, which means "God's House." Before that, the town was called Luz.

Then Jacob made a promise, like a serious vow: "If God sticks with me and keeps me safe on this trip, gives me food and clothes, and gets me back to my dad's house in one piece, then this God will be my God. And this rock I set up? It's gonna be a sign that this is a place where God lives. And out of everything you give me, I'll give a tenth of it back to you."

title: Jacob's Crazy Love Story: 14 Years for Rachel
paragraphs: § Jacob Meets Rachel

So Jacob bounced and headed east. He saw a well in a field with three groups of sheep chilling around it. This well was where everyone got water for their flocks. A massive stone covered the well's opening. The shepherds would only roll the stone away to water the sheep when all the flocks were there, and then they'd put it back.
Jacob walked up and said, "'Sup, guys. Where are you from?"
They replied, "We're from Haran."
Jacob asked, "You know Laban, Nahor's son?"
“Yeah, we know him.”
“Is he doing good?” Jacob asked.
“Totally,” they said. “And look, here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
Jacob was like, “It's still pretty early, the sun's high up. Isn't it too soon to bring the sheep in? Why not water them and let them graze some more?”
“We can't,” they explained. “We have to wait for all the other shepherds. It takes all of us to move that huge stone. Only then can we water the flocks.”

While they were talking, Rachel showed up with her dad's sheep. She was the one taking care of them. The second Jacob saw Rachel, his uncle's daughter, with his uncle's sheep, he went over and, all by himself, rolled the stone away from the well and watered his uncle Laban's flock. Then he kissed Rachel and just started crying. He told her he was her dad's relative, Rebekah's son. She immediately ran and told her father.
When Laban heard the news about his sister's son, Jacob, he ran out to meet him. He gave him a big hug and a kiss and brought him home. Jacob told Laban his whole story.
Laban was like, “You're for real family! My own flesh and blood!”
§ Jacob Gets Tricked
After Jacob had stayed with him for a month, Laban said, “Look, just because you're my nephew doesn't mean you should work for free. Tell me what you want. What's a fair wage?”

Now, Laban had two daughters. The older one was Leah, and the younger one was Rachel. Leah had nice eyes, but Rachel was a total knockout, like, drop-dead gorgeous. And Jacob was completely in love with Rachel.
So Jacob said, “I'll work for you for seven years if I can marry your younger daughter, Rachel.”
Laban replied, “It's way better for me to give her to you than to some random guy. For sure. Stay here with me.”
So Jacob worked for seven years for Rachel. But because he was so in love with her, it felt like only a few days.
Then Jacob went to Laban and said, “I've done my part. Give me my wife. I'm ready to get married.”

So Laban threw a huge party and invited everyone from the area. But when evening came, he brought his daughter Leah to Jacob, and Jacob slept with her. (Laban also gave his servant girl Zilpah to Leah.)
When morning came, Jacob saw it was Leah in his bed!
He went straight to Laban and was like, “What did you do to me?! Didn't I work all this time for Rachel? Why did you trick me?”

Laban answered, “That's not how we do things here. We don't marry off the younger daughter before the older one. Finish the week-long wedding celebration with Leah, and then we'll give you Rachel too. But you'll have to work for me for another seven years.”

Jacob agreed. After the week was over, Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife. (Laban also gave his servant girl Bilhah to Rachel.) So Jacob slept with Rachel, and he loved her way more than Leah. And he worked for Laban for another seven years.
§ The Baby Competition

When God saw that Leah wasn't loved, he made it so she could have kids, but Rachel couldn't. Leah got pregnant and had a son. She named him Reuben, which means “Look, a son!” She said, “This is a sign that God has seen how miserable I am, and now my husband will finally love me.”
She got pregnant again and had another son. She said, “God heard that I was unloved, so he gave me this son too.” She named him Simeon, which means “God heard.”
She got pregnant again and had another son. She said, “Now, for sure, my husband will get attached to me. I've given him three sons!” That's why he was named Levi, which means “attached.”
She got pregnant one last time and had a fourth son. She said, “This time, I'm just going to praise God.” So she named him Judah, which means “praise.” After that, she stopped having kids.

title: Babies, Mandrakes, and a Flock of Riches
paragraphs: § The Baby War Begins
When Rachel realized she wasn't having any kids for Jacob, she got crazy jealous of her sister, Leah. She told Jacob, "You have to give me sons, or I'll literally die!"
Jacob got pretty mad and shot back, "Hey, am I God? I'm not the one stopping you from having babies!"

So Rachel came up with a plan. "Okay, look, here's my servant, Bilhah. Sleep with her. She can be a surrogate for me, and I can start a family through her." So she gave Bilhah to Jacob, and he slept with her. Bilhah got pregnant and had a son for Jacob.
Rachel said, "God totally had my back and proved I was right. He heard me and gave me a son!" So she named him Dan, which means 'Vindicated.'

Then, Rachel's servant Bilhah got pregnant again and gave Jacob a second son. Rachel was like, "I've been in a legit wrestling match with my sister, and I WON." So she named him Naphtali, which means 'My Struggle.'
§ Leah Fights Back
When Leah saw she wasn't having any more kids, she pulled the same move. She gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife. Zilpah had a son for Jacob.
Leah exclaimed, "Wow, so lucky!" and she named him Gad, which means 'Good Fortune.'
When Leah's servant Zilpah had a second son, Leah said, "This is such a happy day! All the women are gonna congratulate me on how happy I am." So she named him Asher, which means 'Happy.'
§ The Mandrake Deal

One day, during the wheat harvest, Leah's son Reuben found some mandrakes in a field and brought them home to his mom. Rachel saw them and asked Leah, "Hey, can I please have some of those mandrakes your son found?"
Leah was not having it. "Wasn't it bad enough that you stole my husband from me? And now you want my son's mandrakes too?"
Rachel shot back, "Fine. Here's the deal: I'll let Jacob sleep with you tonight if you give me your son's mandrakes."
So when Jacob came home from the fields that evening, Leah was waiting for him. "You're sleeping with me tonight. I traded my son's mandrakes for a night with you." So he slept with her that night.
And God listened to Leah. She got pregnant and gave Jacob a fifth son. She said, "God rewarded me for giving my servant to my husband." She named him Issachar, which means 'Reward.'

Leah got pregnant again and had a sixth son for Jacob. She said, "God has given me an awesome gift. This time my husband will finally respect me—I've given him six sons!" So she named him Zebulun, which means 'Honor.'
Finally, she had a daughter and named her Dinah.
§ God Remembers Rachel
Then, God finally remembered Rachel. He listened to her prayers and made it possible for her to have a baby. She got pregnant and had a son!
She said, "God has taken away my shame." She named him Joseph, which means 'Add,' and prayed, "I hope God adds another son to me!"
§ Jacob Wants to Go Home
After Rachel had Joseph, Jacob went to Laban and said, "It's time. Let me go back to my own home. Give me my wives and my kids that I worked for. You know exactly how hard I've worked for you."
Laban replied, "Please, don't go. I had it confirmed by a divine source that God has blessed me like crazy because of you." He added, "So just name your price. Whatever you want, I'll pay you."

Jacob said, "You know firsthand what my work has meant to you and how your livestock have thrived under my care. You had almost nothing when I got here, and now you're loaded. Everything I touched turned into a blessing for you. Isn't it about time I start providing for my own family?"
§ The Deal for the Flock
"Okay, so what should I pay you?" Laban asked.

Jacob answered, "You don't have to pay me anything. But how about this deal? I'll go back to taking care of your flocks. Today, go through all your flocks and pull out every sheep that's speckled or spotted, every dark-colored lamb, and every goat that's spotted or speckled. That will be my payment.
"This way, you can easily check if I'm being honest. Later, when you check on my wages, if you find any goat that isn't speckled or spotted, or any sheep that isn't black, you'll know I stole it."
"Fair enough," said Laban. "It's a deal."
§ Laban's Scheme vs. Jacob's Genius

But that same day, Laban went and removed all the male goats that were mottled and spotted, and all the female goats that were speckled and spotted—basically any animal with a speck of white on it—plus all the black sheep. He put them in his sons' care.
Then he made sure there was a three-day journey separating him from Jacob. Meanwhile, Jacob was left taking care of the rest of Laban's flock.

But Jacob was a genius. He got some fresh branches from poplar, almond, and plane trees and peeled strips of bark off them, creating white stripes. He then stuck these peeled branches in the watering troughs right where the flocks came to drink.
When the animals were in heat, they'd come to drink and end up mating right in front of the striped branches. And guess what? They gave birth to babies that were streaked, spotted, or speckled!
Jacob also separated the ewes and made them face the dark-colored animals from Laban's original flock. By doing this, he created his own distinct flocks that he didn't mix with Laban's.

Whenever the stronger, healthier animals were mating, Jacob would put the branches in the troughs so they'd mate in front of them. But he didn't put the branches out for the weaker animals. This way, the weak animals went to Laban, and all the strong ones went to Jacob.
The guy got richer and richer. He ended up with huge flocks, tons of servants, and a whole lot of camels and donkeys.

title: Jacob's Great Escape and a Tense Family Showdown
paragraphs: § Time to Go Home

Jacob heard that Laban’s sons were trash-talking him. “Jacob totally used our dad’s money to get rich at his expense,” they were saying. At the same time, Jacob noticed Laban was acting super weird toward him, not treating him the same at all. That’s when God told Jacob, “Go back to your homeland. I’ll be with you.”

So Jacob had Rachel and Leah meet him out in the field with his flocks. He said, “I’ve noticed your dad has a major attitude with me; he’s not cool like he was before. But my dad’s God is still with me. You both know how hard I’ve worked for your father. But he has still cheated me over and over, changing my wages whenever he felt like it. But God never let him actually hurt me. If he said, ‘Your pay is the speckled animals,’ the whole flock would have speckled babies. If he said, ‘Your pay is the streaked animals,’ the whole flock would have streaked ones. God kept using your father’s own animals to pay me.

“One time, when the flocks were mating, I had a dream and saw that all the male goats getting busy were streaked, speckled, and mottled. In the dream, an angel of God called out, ‘Jacob!’ I said, ‘What’s up?’ He said, ‘Look closely. All the mating goats are streaked, speckled, and mottled. I know what Laban’s been doing to you. I’m the God of Bethel, where you dedicated that pillar and made a vow to me. Now it’s time to leave. Get out of this place and go back to the land you were born in.’”

Rachel and Leah replied, “Has he treated us any better? We’re basically treated like strangers. All he cared about was the money he got for selling us, and he’s already spent it all. Any of the wealth God took from our father and gave back to us is rightfully ours and our children’s. So just go ahead and do what God told you.”
§ The Great Escape

So Jacob did it. He put his kids and his wives on camels, gathered all his livestock and everything he had acquired in Paddan Aram, and started the journey back home to his father Isaac in the land of Canaan.

While Laban was away shearing his sheep, Rachel stole her father’s household idols. Jacob was so sneaky with his plans that Laban the Aramean had no idea what was happening—he was totally clueless. Jacob got away with everything he owned, crossed the Euphrates River, and headed for the hill country of Gilead.

Three days later, Laban got the news: “Jacob ran off.” Laban gathered his relatives and chased after him. Seven days later, they caught up with him in the hill country of Gilead. That night, God came to Laban in a dream and said, “Be careful. Don’t say anything to Jacob, good or bad.”
§ The Confrontation
When Laban finally reached him, Jacob had his tents set up in the Gilead mountains; Laban and his relatives set up their camp there too.

Laban said to Jacob, “What were you thinking, keeping me in the dark and sneaking off, dragging my daughters away like they’re prisoners of war? Why did you run off like a thief? You should have told me! I would have thrown a huge going-away party with music and celebration! But you didn’t even let me kiss my daughters and grandkids goodbye. That was a really dumb move. I could totally mess you up right now, but the God of your father told me last night, ‘Be careful what you do to Jacob.’ I get it, you were homesick and all. But why did you have to steal my gods?”

Jacob answered, “I was scared. I thought you would just take your daughters from me by force. But about your gods, if you find them with anyone here, that person will die. With everyone watching, search for yourself. If you find anything that’s yours, take it.” (Jacob had no idea that Rachel had stolen them.)

So Laban searched Jacob’s tent, Leah’s tent, and the tents of the two female servants, but found nothing. He went from Leah’s tent to Rachel’s. Rachel had taken the household gods, hidden them in her camel’s saddlebag, and was sitting on them. After Laban had rummaged through the whole tent and found nothing, Rachel said to her father, “Sorry, Dad, don’t be mad that I can’t stand up, but I’m on my period.” So even though he searched everywhere, he couldn’t find his household gods.
§ Jacob's Turn

Now Jacob was furious. He went off on Laban: “So what’s my crime? What did I do wrong that you hunted me down like this? You’ve gone through all my stuff. Did you find a single thing that belongs to you? Put it out here for everyone to see! Let our families be the jury and decide who’s right.

“For the twenty years I worked for you, your sheep and goats never had a miscarriage. I never ate any of the rams from your flock. If an animal was killed by wild beasts, I never brought you the carcass; I took the loss myself. You made me pay for anything stolen, whether it was my fault or not. I worked in scorching heat during the day and freezing cold at night, and I barely got any sleep. I did this for twenty years! I slaved for you for fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flock, and you changed my wages ten times! If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the one Isaac fears, hadn’t been on my side, you would have sent me away with nothing. But God saw my struggle and all my hard work, and last night he made his decision.”
§ The Covenant

Laban shot back, “These daughters are my daughters, these kids are my kids, this flock is my flock—everything you see is mine. But what can I do now about my daughters or the children they’ve had? So let’s make a deal, a covenant between us, and let God be the witness.”

So Jacob took a large stone and set it up as a pillar. He told his relatives, “Gather some stones.” They made a pile of stones and ate a meal there together. Laban named it Yegar-sahadutha (which is Aramaic for “Witness Pile”), and Jacob named it Galeed (which is the Hebrew version).

Laban said, “This pile of stones is a witness between you and me from now on.” That’s why it was called Galeed. It was also called Mizpah (which means “Watchtower”), because Laban said, “May God keep watch between us when we are apart. If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women when no one is around, remember, God is our witness.”

Laban went on, “This pile of stones and this pillar I’ve set up are a witness. I will not cross this line to harm you, and you will not cross this line to harm me. The God of Abraham and the God of Nahor will judge between us.”

Jacob made a promise, swearing by the God his father Isaac feared. Then he offered a sacrifice on the mountain and invited his family to share the meal. They ate together and stayed on the mountain that night. The next morning, Laban got up early, kissed his grandkids and daughters, blessed them, and headed back home.

title: Jacob Wrestles God and Gets a New Name
paragraphs: So Jacob continued his journey, and suddenly, a bunch of God's angels showed up. When Jacob saw them, he was like, “Whoa, God’s squad is here!” So he named the place Mahanaim, which means “Two Camps.”
§ Jacob's Big "Uh Oh" Moment

Jacob sent some messengers ahead to his brother Esau, who was in the Seir region of Edom. He told them, “Give my master Esau this message from your servant Jacob: ‘I’ve been hanging with Laban this whole time and just couldn't get away. I’ve got a ton of cattle, donkeys, sheep, and servants now. I’m just letting you know, hoping you’ll be cool with me.’”
The messengers came back to Jacob and said, “We talked to your brother Esau, and he’s on his way to meet you. But, uh... he’s got 400 men with him.”

Jacob was totally freaking out. Panicked, he split all his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups. His thinking was, “If Esau attacks the first group, at least the other one has a shot at getting away.”
§ The Ultimate Prayer

Then Jacob just prayed his heart out, “God of my grandpa Abraham, God of my dad Isaac, the same God who told me, ‘Go back home, and I’ll take care of you.’ I seriously don’t deserve all the awesome love and faithfulness you’ve shown me. When I left here, I had nothing but the clothes on my back, and now look at me—I’ve got two whole camps! Please, save me from my brother, from my angry brother Esau! I’m terrified he’s going to come and wipe us all out, me, the moms, and the kids. You promised me, ‘I will make sure you’re good; I’ll make your family as huge as the sand on the seashore, too many to even count.’”
§ Operation: Appease Esau

He slept there that night and then got a massive gift ready for his brother Esau from everything he owned: 200 female goats, 20 male goats, 200 ewes, 20 rams, 30 nursing camels with their babies, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 male donkeys. He put a servant in charge of each herd and told them, “Go on ahead of me, but leave some space between each herd.”

He told the first servant, “When my brother Esau meets you and asks, ‘Who’s your boss? Where are you going? Who owns all this?’ you tell him, ‘This all belongs to your servant Jacob. It’s a gift for his master, Esau. And Jacob himself is right behind us.’”

He gave the same instructions to the second and third servants, and to all the others with the herds. He thought, “I’ll chill him out with all these gifts coming one after another. Then, when I see him face-to-face, maybe he’ll actually be happy to see me.” So, the gifts went on ahead, and he stayed in the camp for the night.
§ The Mysterious Wrestling Match
But in the middle of the night, he got up, took his two wives, his two maids, and his eleven kids, and crossed the Jabbok River. He made sure they all got across the river safely with all his stuff.

But Jacob stayed behind by himself. And then some guy started wrestling with him, and they went at it until sunrise. When the guy saw he couldn’t win against Jacob, he touched Jacob’s hip and popped it out of its socket.
The man said, “Let me go, the sun’s coming up.”
But Jacob shot back, “I’m not letting you go until you bless me.”
The man asked, “What’s your name?”
He said, “Jacob.”
Then the man said, “Not anymore. Your name isn’t Jacob anymore. From now on, you’re Israel, which means ‘God-Wrestler,’ because you’ve wrestled with God and with humans, and you’ve won.”
Jacob then asked, “Okay, so what’s your name?”
The man replied, “Why do you even need to know my name?” And right then and there, he blessed him.
§ A New Name and a New Limp
Jacob named that place Peniel, meaning “God’s Face,” because he said, “I saw God face-to-face, and I’m still alive to talk about it! How crazy is that?”

The sun rose just as he was leaving Peniel, and he was limping because of his hip. That’s why, to this day, the people of Israel don’t eat the muscle on the hip socket, because that’s where Jacob was injured.

title: Jacob and Esau: The Ultimate Reunion
paragraphs: § The Reunion

Jacob looked up and boom, there was Esau, rolling up with 400 guys. Jacob quickly split up his kids with Leah, Rachel, and the two maids. He put the maids and their kids in the front, Leah and her kids in the middle, and Rachel and Joseph at the back.

Jacob went ahead of everyone. As he got closer to his brother, he bowed down seven times to show respect. But Esau just ran to him, threw his arms around him, and kissed him. They both started crying, for real.
§ Family Introductions

Then Esau looked around at the women and kids and was like, "Yo, who's all this with you?"
Jacob said, "These are the kids God was awesome enough to give me."
So the maids and their kids came up and bowed. Then Leah and her kids did the same. Finally, Joseph and Rachel came up and bowed to Esau.
§ What's With All the Gifts?

Esau then asked, "So what was up with all those herds of animals I saw on the way?"
Jacob was like, "I was kinda hoping they'd make you happy to see me."
But Esau said, "Bro, for real, I have more than enough. Keep your stuff."

Jacob said, "No, please, for real. If you're actually cool with me, take these gifts. Seeing your face is like seeing God's face smiling at me. Seriously, take them. God's been so good to me, I have everything I need." Jacob kept insisting, so Esau finally took the gifts.
§ Going Their Separate Ways
Then Esau said, "Alright, let's get going. I'll lead the way."

But Jacob said, "My dude, you can see the kids are tired. Plus, the animals are nursing, so we gotta go slow. If I push them too hard for even one day, they'll all die. So, how about you go on ahead, and I'll just take it easy at my own pace with the flocks and the kids. I'll meet you in Seir."

Esau was like, "Okay, but at least let me leave some of my guys with you."
"Nah, it's all good," Jacob said. "You being cool with me is all I need."
So Esau headed back to Seir that day.
§ Jacob's New Crib
And Jacob left for a place called Succoth. He built a house for himself and some sheds for his animals. That's why they called the place Succoth, which means "Sheds."

After all that, Jacob finally made it to Shechem in Canaan, all the way from Paddan Aram, totally safe. He set up his camp near the city. He bought the piece of land where he pitched his tent from the sons of Hamor, who was Shechem's dad. It cost him a hundred silver coins. Then he built an altar there and called it El-Elohe-Israel, which means "The God of Israel is freaking awesome."

title: A Bloody Revenge for a Sister's Honor
paragraphs: § A Terrible Day

So one day, Dinah, the daughter Jacob had with Leah, went to hang out with some of the local women. But then this guy Shechem, the son of the local chief Hamor the Hivite, saw her and did something awful—he assaulted and raped her. After that, he got this intense crush on Dinah, fell totally in love, and tried to get her to like him back. He even went to his dad, Hamor, and said, 'You have to get me this girl for my wife.'

Jacob found out that his daughter Dinah had been raped, but his sons were out in the fields with the animals, so he kept quiet until they came home. In the meantime, Shechem's father, Hamor, came over to Jacob's to try and arrange the marriage. When Jacob's sons got back from the fields and heard the news, they were furious. They were absolutely raging. What Shechem did to Jacob's daughter was a huge deal in Israel, something totally unacceptable that you just don't let slide.
§ A Desperate Deal

Hamor tried to smooth things over with Jacob and his sons. 'My son Shechem is head over heels for your daughter,' he said. 'Please let him marry her. Let's connect our families. You give us your daughters, we'll give you ours. You can live here with us, become one big family. Settle down, make yourselves at home, and get rich with us.'

Then Shechem himself jumped in, talking to Dinah's dad and brothers: 'Please, just say yes. I'll pay whatever you want. Name your price for the bride, seriously, the sky's the limit! Just please, give me this girl as my wife.'
§ The Brothers' Deception

But Jacob's sons were clever and tricky in their reply to Shechem and his father. After all, their sister had been brutally violated. They said, 'That's impossible. We could never give our sister to a guy who isn't circumcised. That would be a complete disgrace for us. The only way we can even talk about this is if all your men get circumcised, just like us. If you do that, then we can trade daughters in marriage, live with you, and become one big happy family. But if you refuse, we're taking our sister and leaving.'

This sounded like a fair deal to Hamor and his son Shechem. The young guy was so obsessed with Jacob's daughter that he immediately agreed to do it. He was also the most respected son in his whole family.

So Hamor and Shechem went to the city gate and pitched the idea to the town leaders: 'These guys are cool with us, they're friendly. Let's let them settle here and live among us; there's plenty of space for them. And think about it, we can marry their daughters! But, there's one condition for them to live with us and become one family: all of our men have to get circumcised, just like them. This is actually a sweet deal for us—these people are loaded, with tons of animals and wealth, and we'll get a piece of that. So let's just agree to their terms and have them move in.'
All the important people in the city agreed with Hamor and Shechem, and every single male in the city was circumcised.
§ Bloody Revenge

Three days after the circumcision, when all the men were still in a lot of pain and recovering, two of Jacob's sons, Simeon and Levi—Dinah's brothers—grabbed their swords, walked straight into the city like they owned the place, and murdered every single man. They killed Hamor and his son Shechem too, rescued Dinah from Shechem's house, and got out of there.

When the rest of Jacob's sons arrived at the massacre, they looted the entire city as payback for what happened to Dinah. They took everything—flocks, herds, donkeys, all their stuff, anything in the city or the fields. They captured all the women and children and took everything valuable from their homes.

Jacob was horrified and said to Simeon and Levi, 'You've ruined my reputation with everyone who lives here, the Canaanites and Perizzites. They'll see me as a monster. We're so few, if they team up and attack us, we're done for. They'll wipe me and my entire family off the face of the earth.'
But they just shot back, 'So we're supposed to let someone treat our sister like an immoral woman and get away with it?'

title: Jacob's Crew, New Names, and More Drama
paragraphs: § Back to Bethel
God told Jacob, "Yo, head back to Bethel. Settle down there and build an altar for the God who showed up for you when you were running from your brother Esau."

So Jacob told his whole crew, "Alright everyone, toss out all those weird foreign gods you've got. Take a shower, put on some fresh clothes. We're heading to Bethel. I'm building an altar there for the God who had my back when I was in major trouble and has been with me this whole time."

They handed over all their foreign god statues and even their lucky charm earrings. Jacob buried all of it under a big oak tree in Shechem. Then they bounced. A crazy fear came over all the towns around them, so nobody even tried to chase after Jacob's sons.

Jacob and his squad finally rolled into Luz (aka Bethel) in Canaan. He built an altar and named it El-Bethel, which means 'God of Bethel,' because that's where God first appeared to him when he was escaping his brother.
§ A Sad Goodbye and a New Name
And that's when Rebekah's old nanny, Deborah, passed away. They buried her just outside Bethel under an oak tree, and they named it "Weeping Oak."

Then God showed up to Jacob again, right after he got back from Paddan Aram, and gave him a blessing. "Your name is Jacob, which means 'Heel-grabber,' but not anymore. From now on, you're Israel, which means 'God-Wrestler.'"

God went on, "I'm the Almighty God. Have a ton of kids! Grow your family! A whole nation, even a bunch of nations, will come from you. Kings will be your descendants. The land I promised to Abraham and Isaac, I'm giving it to you now, and I'll pass it on to your kids after you."
Then God was gone, just like that, ascending from the spot where he'd been talking to him.
Jacob set up a stone pillar right where God had spoken to him. He poured a drink offering on it and anointed it with oil. Jacob named the place Bethel, which means 'God's House.'
§ A Tragic Birth

They left Bethel. They were still a good ways from Ephrath when Rachel went into labor, and it was a really, really tough one. When the contractions were at their absolute worst, the midwife told her, "Don't worry, you've got another son!"
With her last breath, because she was dying, she named him Ben-oni, which means 'Son of My Pain.' But his dad named him Benjamin, which means 'Son of Good Fortune.'
Rachel died and was buried on the road to Ephrath, which is now Bethlehem. Jacob put up a pillar to mark her grave. It's still there today, known as "Rachel's Grave Stone."
§ Family Drama and a Full House
Israel kept moving and set up camp at Migdal Eder. While they were living in that area, Reuben went and slept with his father's concubine, Bilhah. And yeah, Israel heard all about it.
Jacob had twelve sons in total.
The sons from Leah were: Reuben (the firstborn), Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
The sons from Rachel were: Joseph and Benjamin.
The sons from Bilhah, Rachel's servant, were: Dan and Naphtali.
The sons from Zilpah, Leah's servant, were: Gad and Asher.
These were all of Jacob's sons, born to him in Paddan Aram.
§ The End of an Era

Finally, Jacob made it back home to his father Isaac at Mamre in Kiriath Arba, which is now Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac had both lived. Isaac was 180 years old by then. He took his last breath and died, an old man who had lived a long life. His sons, Esau and Jacob, buried him with his family.

title: Esau's Family Tree: The Whole Squad
paragraphs: Here’s the rundown on Esau's family, also known as Edom.
§ Esau's Wives and Kids

First off, Esau married some local girls from Canaan. There was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; Oholibamah, who was the daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite; and Basemath, Ishmael’s daughter and sister of Nebaioth.
Adah had a son named Eliphaz. Basemath had Reuel. And Oholibamah had Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These were Esau's sons, all born in Canaan.

Later on, Esau packed up everything—his wives, kids, all the people in his household, his livestock, and all the stuff he had gathered in Canaan—and moved a good distance away from his brother Jacob. They just had way too much stuff to live in the same area, and the land couldn't support all their animals. So, Esau ended up settling in the hill country of Seir. Just so you know, Esau and Edom are the same guy.
§ Esau's Descendants, The Edomites

So, this is the official family tree of Esau, the guy who started the Edomite nation in the hill country of Seir. The names of Esau’s sons were Eliphaz (from his wife Adah) and Reuel (from his wife Basemath).
Eliphaz’s sons were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz. Eliphaz also had a son named Amalek with his concubine Timna. These were all grandsons of Esau through his wife Adah.
Reuel’s sons were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the grandsons of Esau through his wife Basemath.
Esau’s wife Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah (who was the son of Zibeon), gave him three sons: Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
§ The Chieftains from Esau

These are the leaders, or chieftains, that came from Esau's family. From Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn, came the chieftains Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz, Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These were all leaders in the land of Edom, all descended from Adah.
From Reuel, Esau's son, came the chieftains Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These guys were the leaders from Reuel's line in Edom, all descended from Basemath.
And from Esau's wife Oholibamah came the chieftains Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
So yeah, these are the sons of Esau (aka Edom) and their main leaders.
§ The Original People of Seir

Now, here's the family tree of Seir the Horite, the people who were living in that land originally: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These were the chieftains of the Horites in the land of Edom.

Lotan’s sons were Hori and Homam, and his sister was Timna. Shobal’s sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam. Zibeon’s sons were Aiah and Anah. This is the same Anah who randomly found hot springs in the desert while he was out watching his dad's donkeys. Pretty cool find.

The children of Anah were Dishon and his daughter Oholibamah. The sons of Dishon were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Keran. The sons of Ezer were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan. The sons of Dishan were Uz and Aran.
These were the original Horite chieftains, clan by clan, in the land of Seir.
§ The Kings of Edom

Check it out, these are the kings who ruled in Edom way before Israel even had a king. First up was King Bela, son of Beor, from the city of Dinhabah. When he died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah took over. After Jobab, Hushan from the land of the Temanites became king. When Hushan died, the next king was Hadad son of Bedad. He was a legend who defeated the Midianites in Moab. His city was Avith. After Hadad, Samlah of Masrekah became king. When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth-on-the-River was the new king. After Shaul, Baal-Hanan son of Acbor ruled. And when Baal-Hanan died, Hadad became king. His city was Pau, and his wife was Mehetabel.
§ All The Edomite Chieftains

And finally, here's the full list of chieftains from Esau's line, sorted by their clans and regions: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth, Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon, Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar, Magdiel, and Iram. These were all the chieftains of Edom in their territories.
So there you have it. The complete family history of Esau, the ancestor of all the Edomites.

title: Joseph's Dreams Get Him Into Big Trouble
paragraphs: Jacob's family had settled in Canaan, the same place his dad, Isaac, had lived. This is where the story of Jacob’s family really kicks off.
§ Joseph the Dreamer

It all started with Joseph, who was seventeen. He was out with his brothers, who were shepherds. These were his half-brothers, the sons of his dad’s other wives, Bilhah and Zilpah. Joseph wasn't a snitch, but he did tell his dad about some of the dumb stuff his brothers were doing.

Now, their dad, Israel, loved Joseph more than any of his other kids because he was born when he was an old man. He even had a super fancy, colorful coat made just for him. When his brothers saw how much their dad favored Joseph, they got super jealous and started hating on him. They wouldn't even talk to him.

Then Joseph had a dream, and when he told his brothers about it, they hated him even more. "Yo, check out this crazy dream I had," he said. "We were all in a field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly, my bundle stood up straight, and all of your bundles gathered around and bowed down to mine."
His brothers were like, "Seriously? You think you're going to be our king and boss us around?" That just made them hate him more, because of his dreams and the arrogant way he talked about them.
But it didn't stop there. Joseph had another dream and, of course, he told his brothers all about it. "I had another dream! This time, the sun, the moon, and eleven stars were all bowing down to me."

When he told his dad and brothers, his dad was like, "What is with all these dreams? You think me, your mom, and all your brothers are going to bow down to you?" His brothers were officially jealous, but his dad couldn't stop thinking about it.
§ The Betrayal
One day, Joseph's brothers went to a place called Shechem to let their dad's sheep graze. So, Israel said to Joseph, "Your brothers are in Shechem with the flocks. I need you to go check on them."
"I'm on it," Joseph said.
"Go see how your brothers and the sheep are doing, and then come back and tell me," his dad said. And with that, he sent Joseph off from the Hebron Valley toward Shechem.
Joseph was wandering around the fields when a man found him and asked, "What are you looking for?"
"I'm looking for my brothers," Joseph said. "Do you know where they're grazing their flocks?"
"They're not here anymore," the man said. "I heard them say they were going to Dothan." So Joseph went after his brothers and found them in Dothan.

They saw him coming from a long way off, and by the time he got there, they had already come up with a plan to kill him. "Here comes the dreamer," they said to each other. "Let's kill him and dump his body in one of these old wells. We can just say a wild animal got him. Then we'll see what happens to his precious dreams."

But Reuben, the oldest brother, heard them and tried to save Joseph. "We're not going to kill him," he said. "No bloodshed. Just throw him in this well out here in the middle of nowhere, but don't hurt him." Reuben was secretly planning to come back later, rescue Joseph, and take him back to their dad.
When Joseph got to his brothers, they ripped off his fancy coat, grabbed him, and threw him into the well. It was completely dry; there was no water in it.

Then they all sat down to eat. As they were eating, they saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded up with spices and perfumes to sell in Egypt. That's when Judah said, "Guys, what do we get out of killing our brother and hiding the body? Let's just sell him to these Ishmaelites. At least we won't have killed him. He's our brother, our own flesh and blood, after all." And his brothers actually agreed.
Just then, some Midianite traders passed by. So the brothers pulled Joseph out of the well and sold him for twenty pieces of silver to the Ishmaelites, who took him with them to Egypt.
Later, Reuben came back to the well, and Joseph was gone! He tore his clothes, totally freaking out. He went to his brothers and said, "The boy is gone! What am I going to do?"
They took Joseph's fancy coat, killed a goat, and dipped the coat in its blood. Then they took the coat back to their dad and said, "We found this. Take a look. Is this your son's coat?"
He recognized it right away. "It's my son's coat! A wild animal must have eaten him. Joseph has been torn to pieces!"

Jacob tore his clothes in grief, put on some rough clothes, and mourned for his son for a very long time. His other sons and daughters tried to comfort him, but he wouldn't listen. "I'll be mourning for my son until the day I die," he said. He just couldn't stop crying for him.
Meanwhile, in Egypt, the Midianites sold Joseph to Potiphar, who was one of Pharaoh's officials and the captain of his guard.

title: A Wild Family Scandal and a Clever Plan
paragraphs: § Judah's Family Drama

So, around that time, Judah decided to leave his brothers and go hang out with this guy from Adullam named Hirah. While he was there, he met a Canaanite girl, the daughter of a man named Shua. He married her, they hooked up, and she had a son named Er. Then she got pregnant again and had another son, Onan. After that, she had one more son and named him Shelah. They were living in a place called Kezib when he was born.
Judah found a wife for his first son, Er. Her name was Tamar. But Er, Judah's oldest, did something that really ticked God off, so God ended his life. Not cool.
§ Onan's Selfish Move

So Judah told his second son, Onan, "Dude, you gotta sleep with your brother's widow. It's your duty to make sure your brother has kids to carry on his name." But Onan knew the kid wouldn't technically be his, so every time he slept with his brother's widow, he... well, he made sure not to get her pregnant. God was super offended by this and took his life, too. Seriously, not a good look.

Judah, probably freaking out a little, told his daughter-in-law Tamar, "Hey, just go back to your dad's house and live as a widow until my youngest son, Shelah, grows up." He was secretly worried Shelah would end up dead like his brothers. So Tamar went back home.
§ Tamar's Crazy Plan
Time went by, and Judah's wife, Shua's daughter, died. After the mourning period was over, Judah and his buddy Hirah went to a town called Timnah for the sheep shearing festival.

Someone told Tamar, "Yo, your father-in-law is heading to Timnah to shear his sheep." This was her chance. She took off her widow's clothes, put on a veil so no one would recognize her, and sat by the entrance to Enaim, which was on the way to Timnah. She had figured out that even though Shelah was all grown up, she was never going to get to marry him.
Judah saw her sitting there and, because of the veil, thought she was an immoral woman. He walked over to her and said, "Hey, let's do this." He had zero clue it was his own daughter-in-law.
She played it cool and asked, "What's in it for me?"
He said, "I'll send you a young goat from my flock."
She replied, "Okay, but you have to give me something as a promise until you send it."
"What do you want as a promise?" he asked.
She said, "Your seal, your cord, and that staff you're carrying." He handed them over, they slept together, and she got pregnant.
Afterward, she went home, took off the veil, and put her widow's clothes back on.
§ The Big Reveal

Judah sent the goat with his friend Hirah to get his stuff back from the woman, but Hirah couldn't find her. He asked the local guys, "Where's the immoral woman that usually hangs out by the road near Enaim?"
They were like, "Uh, there's never been an immoral woman here, dude."
So Hirah went back to Judah and said, "I couldn't find her. The locals said there's never been an immoral woman there."
Judah was like, "Whatever, just let her keep the stuff. If we keep looking, we'll just become a joke. I sent the goat, but you couldn't find her. My part's done."
About three months later, someone told Judah, "Your daughter-in-law Tamar has been acting like a total immoral woman, and now she's pregnant."
Judah was furious and yelled, "Get her out here! We're gonna burn her!"
But as they were dragging her out, she sent a message to her father-in-law. It said, "I'm pregnant by the man who owns these things. Take a good look. Who owns this seal, this cord, and this staff?"
Judah recognized them immediately. He said, "She's right, and I'm wrong. I'm the one who didn't let her marry my son Shelah." And he never slept with her again.
§ A Tale of Two Twins

When it was time for her to give birth, surprise! She was having twins. As she was in labor, one of the babies stuck his hand out. The midwife tied a red thread around his wrist and said, "This one's coming out first!" But then he pulled his hand back in, and his brother came out first. The midwife was like, "Whoa, a total breakout!" So they named him Perez, which means "Breakout." Then his brother, the one with the red thread on his hand, was born. They named him Zerah, which means "Bright."

title: Joseph's Unfair Punishment But God's Perfect Plan
paragraphs: § Joseph Gets a New Boss

So after Joseph got taken to Egypt, this dude Potiphar, who was one of Pharaoh's head honchos, bought him. And what do you know, God was totally on Joseph's side, so things went super well for him. He ended up living in his Egyptian master's house, and his master could tell God was with him, making everything he did a success. Potiphar really liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of everything. Because of Joseph, God blessed Potiphar's whole house and everything he owned. Potiphar didn't have to worry about a thing, except what to eat.
§ A Big Problem

Now, Joseph was a really good-looking guy. And after a while, his master's wife started crushing on him hard. One day she just said, 'Sleep with me.' But Joseph refused. He told her, 'Look, my master trusts me with everything. He's put me in charge of his whole household. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, because you're his wife. How could I do something that terrible and sin against God?' She kept asking him day after day, but he wouldn't do it.
§ The Setup

One day, Joseph went into the house to do his work, and none of the other servants were around. She grabbed his coat and said, 'Sleep with me!' But he slipped out of his coat and ran outside. When she saw he'd left his coat, she called the servants and made up a crazy story. 'Look! This Hebrew guy tried to assault me! I screamed, and he ran away, leaving his coat.'
§ Thrown in Jail

She kept the coat until her husband came home and told him the same lie. Her husband got furious and threw Joseph in the jail where the king's prisoners were kept. But even in jail, God was with Joseph. He was kind to him and made the head jailer like him. The jailer put Joseph in charge of all the other prisoners, and he basically ran the whole place. The jailer never had to check on him because God was with him, making sure whatever he did turned out right.

title: Dreams, Drama, and a Forgotten Promise
paragraphs: So, after a while, the king of Egypt's personal drink server and his main baker messed up and made their boss, the king, super mad. Pharaoh was so ticked off at them that he threw them in the same jail where Joseph was, under the watch of the captain of the guard. The captain put Joseph in charge of them.
§ Bummer Dreams in Jail

After they'd been locked up for a bit, both the cupbearer and the baker had these intense dreams on the same night, and each dream felt like it meant something specific. When Joseph came to check on them in the morning, he saw they were totally bummed out. He asked them, 'What's up? Why the long faces?'
They were like, 'We both had these crazy dreams, but there's no one to tell us what they mean.' Joseph replied, 'Doesn't God know what dreams mean? Just tell me what you dreamed.'
§ The Cupbearer's Dream

So the head cupbearer went first. 'Okay, so in my dream, there was this vine right in front of me with three branches. It grew buds, then flowers, and then boom—ripe grapes. I was holding Pharaoh's cup, so I grabbed the grapes, squeezed the juice into his cup, and handed it to him.'

Joseph was like, 'Alright, here's the deal. The three branches are three days. In three days, Pharaoh's gonna let you out and give you your old job back. You'll be handing him his cup just like you used to. Just, when things are good for you again, please remember me. Tell Pharaoh about me and get me out of this place. I was literally kidnapped from my home, and I've done nothing to deserve being stuck in this hole.'
§ The Baker's Dream

When the head baker saw how well that went, he was like, 'My turn! My dream was like this: I had three big baskets stacked on my head. The top one was full of all kinds of pastries for the king, but birds were flying down and eating them right out of the basket.'

Joseph’s face fell. 'Man, this is what it means: The three baskets are also three days. In three days, Pharaoh is going to chop off your head, stick you on a pole, and birds will eat your body. It's grim, I know.'
§ A Forgotten Promise

And for real, three days later it was Pharaoh's birthday, and he threw a huge party for his whole staff. He brought out the cupbearer and the baker and put them in front of everyone. He gave the cupbearer his old job back, and he was serving Pharaoh his wine again. But then, he had the baker executed and impaled on a post, exactly like Joseph said would happen.
But the head cupbearer? He totally spaced on Joseph. He forgot all about him.

title: Pharaoh's Wild Dreams and Joseph's Big Break
paragraphs: § Pharaoh's Crazy Dreams

So, like, two whole years went by, and Pharaoh had this wild dream. He was just chilling by the Nile River when, boom, seven super healthy-looking cows came right out of the water and started munching on the grass.

But then, right after them, seven other cows that were basically just skin and bones came out of the river. They stood next to the healthy cows, and then—get this—the skinny cows straight up ate the seven healthy ones. Pharaoh woke up, totally weirded out.

He fell back asleep and had another dream. This time, he saw seven ears of corn, all plump and perfect, growing on one stalk. Then, seven more ears grew, but these were all thin and dried up. And just like before, the thin, nasty ears of corn swallowed the healthy ones. Pharaoh woke up again like, "Whoa, another dream."
§ The Search for an Interpreter
The next morning, Pharaoh was seriously bugged. He called all the magicians and wise guys in Egypt and told them his dreams, but nobody had a clue what they meant. They were all stumped.

That's when the head cupbearer finally spoke up. "My bad, Pharaoh," he said. "I totally forgot to tell you something. A while back, you were mad at me and the head baker and threw us in jail. We both had these crazy dreams on the same night, and each dream meant something different.

"There was this young Hebrew guy in there with us, a slave of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams, and he explained them to us, like, perfectly. And everything happened exactly like he said it would. I got my job back, and the baker got... well, executed."
§ Joseph Gets Called Up
Pharaoh was like, "Get me that guy, NOW!" So they rushed Joseph out of his prison cell. He got a haircut, changed into some clean clothes, and went to see the king.
"I had a dream," Pharaoh told Joseph, "and no one can figure it out. But I heard that you can interpret dreams just by hearing them."
"Nah, it's not me," Joseph said. "But God will give you the answer and put your mind at ease."
§ Pharaoh Spills the Tea

So Pharaoh told Joseph the whole story. "In my dream, I was by the Nile, and seven healthy, fat cows came out and started grazing. Then seven more cows, super skinny and ugly—like, the ugliest I've ever seen in Egypt—came up after them. And the skinny cows ate the fat ones, but you couldn't even tell! They were still just as skinny and ugly as before. Then I woke up.

"In my second dream, I saw seven full, healthy ears of grain on one stalk. Then seven more shriveled, thin ears grew. And the thin ears swallowed the good ones. I told all my magicians, but they're clueless."
§ Joseph's Epic Interpretation

Joseph told Pharaoh, "Dude, both your dreams mean the exact same thing. God is giving you a heads-up about what's about to happen. The seven healthy cows are seven years, and the seven healthy ears of grain are also seven years. It's the same message.
"The seven sick, ugly cows that came after are seven years, and the seven dried-up ears of grain are seven years of famine. A huge food shortage.

"So, here's the deal: God is showing you His plan. There are going to be seven years of insane abundance all over Egypt. But right after that, seven years of a terrible famine will hit. It'll be so bad that everyone will forget how good the plentiful years were. The famine will completely wreck the country.
"The reason you dreamed it twice is because God is 100% serious about this, and it's going to happen really soon."
§ Joseph's Master Plan

"So, here's what you should do," Joseph continued. "You need to find a really smart and wise dude and put him in charge of the whole country. Then, appoint managers all over Egypt to collect food during the seven good years.

"Their job is to gather up all the extra food and store it in cities under your authority. That way, when the seven years of famine come, you'll have a massive stockpile of food saved up, and the country won't be totally destroyed."
Pharaoh and his whole crew thought this was a brilliant idea. Total genius.
§ From Prisoner to Prince
Pharaoh said to his officials, "Could we find anyone better for this job? This guy literally has the Spirit of God in him!"

So Pharaoh turned to Joseph and said, "Since God has shown you all this, there's no one smarter or wiser than you. You're the man. From now on, you're in charge of my palace, and all my people will answer to you. The only person with more power than you will be me, the king."

Then Pharaoh made it official. "I'm putting you in charge of all of Egypt." He took off his special royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He dressed him in super fancy clothes and put a gold chain around his neck. He even gave him the second-best chariot to ride in, and people shouted "Bow down!" as he passed.
Pharaoh told him, "I'm Pharaoh, but for real, nobody in Egypt is going to lift a hand or a foot without your okay."

Then Pharaoh gave Joseph an Egyptian name, Zaphenath-Paneah, which means "God Speaks and He Lives." He also gave him a wife, Asenath, whose dad was a priest in the city of On. And just like that, Joseph was running the whole country.
Joseph was thirty years old when he started working for Pharaoh. He left the king's presence and immediately started organizing all of Egypt.
§ The Good Times and the Bad

For the next seven years, the land produced a crazy amount of food. It was a total boom. Joseph collected all the surplus food and stored it in the cities. He gathered so much grain it was like counting the sand on the beach. Eventually, he just stopped keeping track because there was too much.

Before the famine started, Joseph and his wife Asenath had two sons. He named the first one Manasseh, which means "Forget," because he said, "God made me forget all my suffering and my family back home." He named the second one Ephraim, meaning "Double Prosperity," saying, "God has made me successful in this land where I've suffered so much."
Then, just as Joseph predicted, the seven years of plenty ended, and the seven years of famine began. The famine hit every country, but thanks to Joseph, Egypt was the only place that had food.
When the people of Egypt started running out of food, they cried to Pharaoh for help. Pharaoh told them, "Go to Joseph. Do whatever he says."

The famine got worse and worse everywhere. So Joseph opened up the storehouses and started selling grain to the Egyptians. And it wasn't just them—people from all over the world started coming to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph because the famine was that bad everywhere else. It was a global crisis.

title: Joseph's Brothers Face a Surprise Test
paragraphs: When Jacob found out there was food in Egypt, he was like, 'Guys, why are you just sitting around staring at each other? I heard there's food in Egypt. Get down there and buy some so we don't starve.'

So, ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to get food. But Jacob didn't let Joseph's younger brother, Benjamin, go with them. He was scared something bad might happen to him. So, the sons of Israel went with everyone else to Egypt to buy food because the famine was hitting Canaan hard, too.
§ Joseph's Surprise Reunion

Joseph was basically running the show in Egypt, handing out food to everyone. When his brothers showed up, they bowed down to him, showing major respect. Joseph knew who they were right away, but he acted like they were total strangers and was harsh with them.
He asked, 'Where are you from?'
'From Canaan,' they replied. 'We're here to buy food.'
Joseph knew it was them, but they had no clue who he was. He remembered the dreams he had about them and said, 'You're spies! You're here to find our weak spots.'
'No way, sir,' they said. 'We're just here to buy food. We're all brothers from the same family. We're honest guys, we'd never spy on you.'
'Nah, you're spies,' he insisted. 'You're here to check out our weaknesses.'
They explained, 'There were twelve of us brothers, all sons of the same dad in Canaan. The youngest is back home with our father, and one of us is... gone.'

But Joseph wasn't buying it. 'It's just like I said, you're spies. And here's how I'm gonna prove it. I swear by the Pharaoh, you're not leaving this place until your younger brother gets here. One of you has to go get him while the rest of you stay in jail. We'll see if you're telling the truth. I swear by the Pharaoh, you're spies.'
And with that, he threw them in jail for three days.
§ The Test

On the third day, Joseph told them, 'Do this and you'll live. I'm a man who fears God. If you're as honest as you claim, one of you will stay here in jail while the rest of you take food back to your starving families. But you have to bring your youngest brother back to me. That'll prove you're telling the truth, and you won't die.' They agreed.

Then they started talking to each other, saying, 'This is payback for what we did to our brother. We saw how scared he was when he begged for mercy, but we didn't listen. Now we're the ones in deep trouble.'
Reuben jumped in, 'Didn't I tell you not to hurt the kid? But you wouldn't listen. And now we're paying for his murder.'

Joseph had been using an interpreter, so they didn't know he understood every word. He had to turn away from them and cry. When he got himself together, he took Simeon and had him tied up right in front of them.
Then Joseph ordered his servants to fill their sacks with grain, put their money back in each sack, and give them food for their journey. It was all done for them.
They loaded up their donkeys with the food and left.
§ The Money's Back?

When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to feed his donkey and found his money right at the top of the bag. He yelled to his brothers, 'My money's back! It's right here in my bag!' They were all confused and scared. 'What is God doing to us?' they wondered.

When they got back to their father, Jacob, in Canaan, they told him everything that had happened. 'The man in charge of the country was really rough with us and accused us of being spies. We told him, 'We're honest guys, not spies. There were twelve of us brothers, sons of one father. One is gone, and the youngest is with our dad in Canaan.'

'But the man in charge said, 'Leave one of your brothers with me, take food for your starving families, and go. Bring your youngest brother back to me to prove you're honest and not spies. Then I'll give your brother back to you, and you can come and go as you please in this country.''
As they were emptying their sacks, each man found his pouch of money. When they and their father saw the money, they were all freaked out.
Their father, Jacob, said to them, 'You're taking everything from me! Joseph is gone, Simeon is gone, and now you want to take Benjamin. You're going to leave me with nothing!'
Reuben spoke up, 'I'll give you my two sons as hostages. If I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill them. Trust me with him; I'll bring him back.'
But Jacob refused. 'My son is not going with you. His brother is dead, and he's all I have left. If something bad happens to him on the way, you'll be the death of me.'

title: The Brothers Face the Music in Egypt
paragraphs: § Back to Egypt, But With a Catch
The famine was still hitting hard. When Jacob's family finished all the food they'd brought from Egypt, he told his sons, "Go back and get us some more."

But Judah was straight up with him. "Look, Dad, the guy in charge was dead serious. He said, 'You won't even see my face unless you bring your brother with you.' If you let our brother come, we'll go. But if not, we're staying put. It's pointless otherwise. He made it crystal clear."
Israel (that's Jacob) was like, "Why'd you make my life so hard? Did you really have to tell him you had another brother?"

They shot back, "The man was grilling us! He kept asking about our family, like 'Is your dad still alive? Got any other brothers?' We just answered his questions. How were we supposed to know he'd demand we bring him here?"

Judah stepped up to his dad. "Just let the kid come with me. I'll be responsible for him. We gotta go now, or we're all gonna starve—us, you, and all our kids. I swear on my life, I'll keep him safe. If I don't bring him back, I'll take the blame forever. Seriously, if we hadn't wasted all this time arguing, we could've been there and back twice already."
§ The Plan and the Gifts

Finally, their dad Israel caved. "Fine, if that's how it has to be. But here's the plan: pack up the best stuff we have—like balm, honey, spices, perfumes, pistachios, and almonds—and take it as a gift for the man. And take double the money. Pay back what was in your sacks; it was probably a mistake. Now take your brother and go. I pray the big man upstairs shows you some mercy so he sends back your other brother and Benjamin. As for me... I've already lost so much. What's one more?"
So the brothers grabbed the gifts, the extra cash, and Benjamin. They didn't waste any time and headed straight for Egypt to meet Joseph.
§ An Awkward Welcome
When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he told his head servant, "Bring these guys inside. Cook up a big meal. They're eating with me at noon."

The servant did what he was told and led them into the house. But the brothers started freaking out. They were whispering, "It's gotta be about the money from last time. He thinks we stole it. Now he's got us trapped and is gonna make us his slaves and take our donkeys!"

So they pulled the head servant aside at the door. "Excuse me, sir," they said. "We came here once before to buy food. On the way home, we opened our bags and found the exact amount of money we paid right at the top. We brought it all back, plus more to buy food. We have no clue who put the money in our bags."

The servant was chill. "It's all good, don't worry," he said. "Your God, and your father's God, must've slipped you a little bonus. I got your payment in full." Then he brought out their brother, Simeon.
He took them inside, made them feel at home, gave them water to wash their feet, and fed their donkeys. The brothers laid out their gifts and waited for Joseph to show up for their noon meal.
§ The Big Reunion (Almost)
When Joseph got home, they gave him the gifts and bowed down low.
Joseph greeted them, "So, how's that old father you told me about? Is he still alive and well?"
"Yes, sir," they replied. "Your servant, our father, is doing great." And they bowed down again.
Then Joseph spotted his brother Benjamin, his own mom's son. "Is this the youngest brother you told me about?" he asked. Then he said, "God be gracious to you, my son."

Seeing his brother hit him right in the feels, and he was about to start bawling. Joseph rushed out to another room for a good cry. Then he washed his face, got himself together, and came back out, saying, "Let's eat."

Joseph ate at his own table, the brothers had their own, and the Egyptians had theirs (because Egyptians thought eating with Hebrews was gross). The brothers were seated right across from Joseph, lined up from oldest to youngest. They just stared at each other, totally clueless about what was happening.
When the food was served from Joseph's table, Benjamin's plate was piled way higher than anyone else's. And so they all had a feast with Joseph and drank as much as they wanted.
