title: A Brother's Desperate Plea to Save Another
paragraphs: Joseph told his head servant, “Load up their bags with as much food as they can hold, and stick their money back in the top of each bag. And in the youngest one’s bag, put my personal silver cup, right on top of his money.” The servant did exactly what Joseph said.
§ The Chase Is On

As soon as the sun was up, the brothers and their donkeys were on their way. They hadn’t even gotten out of the city when Joseph told his steward, “Go after them! When you catch them, say, ‘Why would you repay good with evil? That cup you took is the one my master drinks from and even uses to figure stuff out. What you did is seriously messed up!’”

The steward caught up and said exactly that. The brothers were like, “Whoa, what are you talking about? We’d never do that! Look, we brought back the money we found in our bags all the way from Canaan. You really think we’d steal from your master now? If you find that cup on any of us, that person can die, and the rest of us will be your master’s slaves.”
The steward replied, “Okay, fine, but let’s not get that extreme. Whoever has the cup will be my slave, but the rest of you are free to go.”
They all rushed to get their bags on the ground and opened them up. The steward searched everything, starting with the oldest and ending with the youngest. And boom—the cup was in Benjamin’s bag.
They completely lost it, tearing their clothes in frustration. They loaded up their donkeys and headed back to the city.
§ The Confrontation
Joseph was still at his house when Judah and his brothers got there. They immediately threw themselves on the ground in front of him.
Joseph hit them with, “How could you do this? You had to know a guy like me would figure this out.”

Judah, speaking for everyone, said, “What can we even say, master? There’s nothing to say. How can we prove we’re innocent? God is the one behind this, showing us how messed up we are. We’re guilty. We’ll be your slaves—all of us, not just the one with the cup.”
“No way, I’d never do that,” Joseph said. “Only the guy who had the cup will be my slave. The rest of you can go back to your father in peace.”
§ Judah's Plea

Judah stepped up and said, “Please, master, can I just say one thing? Please don’t get mad. To me, you’re just as powerful as Pharaoh. You asked us, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’ And we told you the truth, ‘We have an old father, and a younger brother who was born when he was old. His other brother is dead, so he’s the only one left from his mom, and his dad loves him like crazy.’
“Then you told us, ‘Bring him here so I can see him.’ We told you it was impossible, that the boy couldn’t leave his father because his father would die if he did.
“But then you said, ‘If your youngest brother doesn’t come with you, you’ll never see my face again.’

“When we got back to our father, we told him everything you said. So when our dad told us to go buy more food, we had to tell him straight up, ‘We can’t. The only way we can go is if our youngest brother comes with us. We’re not even allowed to see the man unless our youngest brother is there.’

“Our father, your servant, told us, ‘You know my wife gave me two sons. One of them disappeared, and I’m pretty sure he was torn apart by animals. I’ve never seen him since. If you take this one from me too and something bad happens to him, you’ll be sending my grieving, old self to the grave.’

“So, you see, if I go back to my father without the boy—his life is totally wrapped up in this kid’s life—the second he sees the boy isn’t with us, he’ll die. He’ll literally die of grief, and we’ll be the ones who killed him. Plus, I personally guaranteed his safety to my father. I promised him, ‘If I don’t bring him back, I’ll take the blame for the rest of my life.’

“So please, let me stay here as your slave instead of the boy. Let the boy go back with his brothers. How can I possibly go back to my father if the boy isn’t with me? I can’t stand to watch my father die of a broken heart!”

title: The Biggest Plot Twist: Joseph is Alive!
paragraphs: § The Big Reveal

Joseph just couldn’t keep it together anymore in front of all his staff. He yelled, “Everyone get out! I need the room!” So, it was just him and his brothers when he finally told them who he was. He was crying so hard that all the Egyptians heard it, and the news even got back to Pharaoh’s palace.
Joseph said to his brothers, “It’s me, Joseph. Is my dad really still alive?” But his brothers were totally shook. They couldn’t even speak; they were just staring, completely mind-blown.

“Come on, get closer,” Joseph said. So they did. “Yeah, it’s me. I’m your brother, Joseph. The one you sold to Egypt. But hey, don’t beat yourselves up about it. This was all God’s plan. He sent me here ahead of you guys to save lives. We’ve had this crazy famine for two years, and there are still five more to go, with no farming or anything. God sent me here to make sure our family line survives and to pull off this epic rescue mission. So, for real, it wasn’t you who sent me here. It was God. He made me like a father to Pharaoh, put me in charge of his whole house, and made me the ruler of all of Egypt.”
§ The Plan to Bring Jacob to Egypt

“Now, hurry back to my dad and tell him his son Joseph says: ‘God has made me the boss of all of Egypt. Get down here ASAP. You’ll live in Goshen, super close to me—you, your kids, your grandkids, all your animals, everything. I’ll take care of you. We’ve still got five years of this famine left, but I’ll make sure you and your whole crew have everything you need. You won’t lack a thing.’

“Look, you can see it with your own eyes, and my bro Benjamin sees it too—it’s really me telling you all this. Go tell my dad how I’m living large here in Egypt, tell him everything you’ve seen. But don’t waste time—get my dad down here now!”
Then Joseph hugged his brother Benjamin, and they both just cried. Then he kissed all his brothers and cried with them. After that, they finally started talking to him.
When the news hit Pharaoh’s palace that Joseph’s brothers were here, Pharaoh and his whole crew were actually pretty stoked about it.

Pharaoh told Joseph, “Tell your brothers the plan: Load up your animals, go back to Canaan, and bring your dad and your families back here. I’ll give you the best land in Egypt, and you’ll be living the good life.”

“And tell them this, too: ‘Take some wagons from Egypt for your kids and wives, and get your dad and come back. Don’t even worry about the stuff you’re leaving behind, because the best of everything in Egypt is yours for the taking.’”
§ The Journey Home

So that’s exactly what they did. Joseph gave them the wagons Pharaoh promised and a bunch of food for the road. He gave all his brothers brand-new clothes, but he hooked Benjamin up with 300 pieces of silver and a bunch of fresh outfits. And for his dad, he sent ten donkeys loaded with all the best stuff from Egypt, and another ten donkeys loaded with grain, bread, and other food for the trip back.
Then he sent his brothers on their way. As they were leaving, he told them, “Don’t get into any fights on the way back, okay? Just chill.”

They left Egypt and went back to their dad, Jacob, in Canaan. When they told him, “Joseph is alive! And he’s the ruler of all of Egypt!” he was just numb. He couldn’t believe it. But the more they told him everything Joseph had said, and when he saw the wagons Joseph had sent to bring him back, he started to come back to life. His spirit totally revived.
Israel said, “That’s all I needed to hear. My son Joseph is alive. I have to go see him before I die.”

title: The Epic Family Road Trip to Egypt
paragraphs: So, Israel packed up everything he owned and started his journey. He got to Beersheba and took a moment to worship, offering sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.
That night, God spoke to Israel in a vision, calling out, “Jacob! Jacob!”
“Yeah?” he answered. “I’m listening.”

God said, “I am the God of your father. Don’t be scared about going down to Egypt. I’m going to turn you into a huge nation there. I’ll go down to Egypt with you, and I’ll also bring you back. And when you die, Joseph will be right there with you; he’ll be the one to close your eyes.”
§ The Big Move

So Jacob left Beersheba. Israel’s sons loaded up their father, their little kids, and their wives onto the wagons that Pharaoh had sent for him. They rolled into Egypt with all their livestock and the stuff they had gathered in Canaan. Jacob brought his entire family with him—sons and grandsons, daughters and granddaughters. Literally everyone.
§ The Whole Crew
Here’s the list of the Israelites, Jacob and his descendants, who went to Egypt:
Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn. Reuben’s sons were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
Simeon’s sons were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jakin, Zohar, and Shaul, whose mom was a Canaanite woman.
Levi’s sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Judah’s sons were Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah (though Er and Onan had already died back in Canaan). Perez’s sons were Hezron and Hamul.
Issachar’s sons were Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.
Zebulun’s sons were Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
These were the sons Leah had with Jacob in Paddan Aram, plus his daughter Dinah. In total, that’s thirty-three sons and daughters.
Gad’s sons were Zephon, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
Asher’s sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. They also had a sister, Serah. Beriah’s sons were Heber and Malkiel.
These sixteen were the children Jacob had with Zilpah, the servant Laban had given to his daughter Leah.

The sons of Jacob’s wife Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin. Joseph had two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, with his wife Asenath, who was the daughter of Potiphera, a priest of On. They were born in Egypt. Benjamin’s sons were Bela, Beker, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
These fourteen were the children Jacob had through Rachel.
Dan’s son was Hushim.
Naphtali’s sons were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
These seven were the children Jacob had through Bilhah, the servant Laban had given to his daughter Rachel.

All in all, the number of people who went to Egypt with Jacob—his direct descendants, not counting his sons’ wives—was sixty-six. If you add the two sons born to Joseph in Egypt, Jacob’s family in Egypt totaled seventy people.
§ The Reunion

Jacob sent Judah ahead to get directions to Goshen from Joseph. When they arrived in the Goshen area, Joseph got his chariot ready and went to meet his father, Israel. The moment Joseph saw him, he threw his arms around his neck and just wept for a long time.
Israel said to Joseph, “I’m ready to die now. I’ve seen your face—you’re actually alive.”
§ The Game Plan

Joseph then talked to his brothers and his father’s family. “I’ll go and tell Pharaoh, ‘My brothers and my father’s family, who were living in Canaan, have come to me. These guys are shepherds; they’ve always raised livestock for a living. And they’ve brought their flocks, herds, and everything else they own.’ When Pharaoh calls you in and asks what you do for a living, tell him, ‘Your servants have always raised livestock, for as long as we can remember—us and our ancestors too.’ That way, he’ll let you settle in the Goshen area—because Egyptians really look down on shepherds.”

title: Joseph's Family Moves to Egypt
paragraphs: § Family Reunion in Egypt
Joseph went straight to Pharaoh and was like, “My dad and brothers are here from Canaan! They brought all their animals and everything they own. They’re hanging out in Goshen for now.”
He brought five of his brothers to meet Pharaoh. Pharaoh asked them, “So, what do you guys do?”

They replied, “We’re shepherds, just like our ancestors. We came here because the famine in Canaan is insane, and there’s no grass for our flocks. If it’s cool with you, we’d love to settle in Goshen.”

Pharaoh looked at Joseph and said, “Awesome, your family’s here! Egypt is totally open to them. Let them live in Goshen, the best land we have. And hey, if any of them are really good at their job, put them in charge of my own livestock.”
Then, Joseph brought his dad, Jacob, to meet Pharaoh. Jacob gave Pharaoh a blessing, and Pharaoh asked him, “Dang, how old are you?”
Jacob said, “I’ve been wandering for 130 years. It’s been a tough life, and way shorter than my ancestors’ lives.” Then he blessed Pharaoh again and left.

Joseph got his family all set up in Egypt. They got the best land in the region of Rameses, just like Pharaoh ordered. Joseph made sure everyone, from his dad to the youngest kid, had everything they needed.
§ The Famine Gets Real

Eventually, the food ran out everywhere. The famine was no joke, and both Egypt and Canaan were struggling hard. Joseph collected all the money from people buying food and put it in Pharaoh’s treasury.
When everyone’s money was gone, the Egyptians came to Joseph, begging, “We need food! Are you just gonna let us die? We’re totally broke.”

Joseph was like, “Okay, if you’re out of cash, bring me your livestock. I’ll trade you food for them.” So, people brought their horses, sheep, cattle, and donkeys, and Joseph gave them food to get through the year.
§ Land for Food

The next year, they were back. “Sir, you know we’re broke. Our money is gone, and you have our animals. The only things we have left are our bodies and our land. Seriously, are you gonna watch us starve? Let’s make a deal. Take us and our land in exchange for food. We’ll be Pharaoh’s slaves, but at least give us some seeds so we can grow crops and not die.”
So, Joseph bought all the land in Egypt for Pharaoh. Every single Egyptian sold their land because the famine was that bad. Pharaoh ended up owning all the land, and the people became his slaves.
But Joseph didn’t buy the priests’ land. They got a regular allowance from Pharaoh, so they didn’t need to sell.

Then Joseph told the people, “Alright, listen up. I’ve bought you and your land for Pharaoh. Now, I’m giving you seeds to plant. When you harvest the crops, one-fifth of it goes to Pharaoh. You can keep the other four-fifths for yourselves, for seeds and for feeding your families.”
They were all like, “You’re a lifesaver! We’re actually happy to be Pharaoh’s slaves.”
Joseph made it a law in Egypt that a fifth of all produce belongs to Pharaoh. This law is still around today. Only the priests’ land wasn’t owned by Pharaoh.
§ Jacob's Final Request
So the Israelites settled in Goshen, got some property, and their population exploded. Jacob lived in Egypt for 17 years, making his grand total 147 years old.

When Jacob knew he was about to die, he called for Joseph. “Do me a solid. Swear to me you’ll be loyal and won’t bury me in Egypt. When I die, I want you to carry me out of Egypt and bury me with my ancestors.”
Joseph said, “I got you. I’ll do it.”
“Swear to me,” Jacob insisted. And Joseph swore.
Then, from his bed, Jacob bowed his head, grateful and at peace.

title: A Grandfather's Blessing Gets a Plot Twist
paragraphs: A while later, Joseph got the news: "Your dad is sick." So he took his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, and went to see his father. When Jacob was told, "Your son Joseph is here to see you," he rallied and sat up in bed.
§ A Father's Declaration

Jacob said to Joseph, "The Strong God appeared to me at Luz in Canaan and blessed me. He told me, 'I'm going to make you have a huge family, a whole community of people, and I will give this land to your descendants as their permanent property.' Now, listen. Your two sons, who were born here in Egypt before I arrived, I'm adopting them. Ephraim and Manasseh will be my sons, just like Reuben and Simeon are. Any children you have after them will be yours, and they will inherit their property from their older brothers. I'm doing this for your mother, Rachel. It still breaks my heart that she died in the land of Canaan on our journey, just a short distance from Ephrath, which is now Bethlehem."
§ A Grandfather's Blessing
Just then, Jacob noticed Joseph's sons and asked, "Who are these boys?"
Joseph replied, "They are my sons, the ones God has given me in this place."

"Bring them to me so I can bless them," Jacob said. His eyesight was failing from old age, and he could barely see. Joseph brought his sons close, and Jacob kissed and embraced them. He said to Joseph, "I never thought I'd see your face again, and now God has let me see your children too!"

Joseph then moved his sons from Jacob's knees and bowed with his face to the ground. He took Ephraim in his right hand to place him at Jacob's left, and Manasseh in his left hand to place him at Jacob's right. But Jacob crossed his arms, placing his right hand on the head of Ephraim, the younger son, and his left hand on the head of Manasseh, the firstborn. Then he spoke this blessing:

"The God my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked with,
The God who has been my shepherd my entire life,
The Angel who has rescued me from all harm—
bless these boys.
May my name and the names of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac, live on through them.
And may they grow into a huge population on the earth."
§ An Unexpected Switch

When Joseph saw his father place his right hand on Ephraim's head, he was concerned he'd made a mistake. He took his father's hand to move it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's. "No, Father," he said, "this one is the firstborn. Put your right hand on his head."

But his father refused. "I know, my son, I know," he said. "He will also become a people, and he will be great. But his younger brother will be even greater, and his descendants will become a multitude of nations." So he blessed them that day, saying, "In your names, Israel will speak a blessing: 'May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.'" In this way, he put Ephraim ahead of Manasseh.
§ A Final Promise

Then Israel said to Joseph, "I am about to die, but God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your fathers. And to you, as the first among your brothers, I give one more portion of land than your brothers—the portion I captured from the Amorites with my own sword and bow."

title: Jacob's Final Words to His Sons
paragraphs: §Jacob's Last Words
Jacob got all his sons together and was like, “Yo, gather ‘round. I’m about to tell you what’s going to happen to you guys in the future.”
“Come close and listen up, sons of Jacob. Listen to your dad, Israel.”
§Reuben

“Reuben, you’re my oldest, my first kid. You were supposed to be the strongest, the most honored, and the most powerful. But you messed up big time, like spilling a glass of water. You’re not on top anymore. Why? Because you hooked up with one of my wives, disrespecting me and my bed. That was a major fail.”
§Simeon & Levi

“Simeon and Levi, you two are a real piece of work, always ready to throw down. I want nothing to do with your drama or your revenge plots. You guys kill people when you're mad and hurt animals just for fun. Seriously, a curse on your crazy anger. I'm gonna scatter your descendants all over Israel, like they're nothing.”
§Judah

“Judah, you're the man. Your brothers are all gonna look up to you. You'll have your enemies in a chokehold while your own family bows down. You're like a young lion, coming back after a big win. Who would dare mess with a lion just chilling? A true king. The leadership will always belong to your family line. You'll be in charge until the ultimate ruler shows up, and everyone will follow him. You'll be so rich you'll tie your donkey to a fancy grapevine and wash your clothes in wine. Your eyes will be darker than wine, and your teeth whiter than milk. An absolute legend.”
§Zebulun
“Zebulun, you'll set up camp by the sea. Your place will be a safe spot for ships, right next to the big city of Sidon.”
§Issachar

“Issachar is like a super strong donkey just chilling between two saddlebags. He saw that his land was awesome and the country was beautiful, so he basically gave up his freedom to become a slave worker. Not the best trade-off, dude.”
§Dan

“Dan will make sure his people get justice; he’ll totally hold his own among the tribes of Israel. But watch out, Dan is like a sneaky snake hiding in the grass. He'll strike a horse's heel and make its powerful rider fall flat on his face. Ouch.”
§A Prayer
“God, I’m waiting and hoping for you to save us.”
§Gad
“Gad is gonna get jumped by a bunch of raiders, but he’ll get them back in the end.”
§Asher
“Asher’s crew will be known for making amazing food, like fancy desserts that are fit for a king.”
§Naphtali
“Naphtali is like a deer running free, who has beautiful baby deer.”
§Joseph

“Joseph is a total beast, like a wild donkey by a spring, full of energy. His enemies, those haters, came at him hard with their bows and arrows. But he didn't even flinch. He stood his ground, his bow ready, his arms strong, because he had the Champion of Jacob, the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel on his side. The God of your father will help you! The Almighty God will bless you with insane blessings—from the sky above and the earth below. Blessings of having lots of kids and livestock. My blessings for you are even bigger than the blessings of the ancient mountains or the epic hills. May all these blessings land on you, Joseph, because you were the one who stood out among your brothers.”
§Benjamin
“Benjamin is like a starving wolf. He eats his prey all morning, and at night, he shares the leftovers.”
§The End of an Era
These were the twelve tribes of Israel, and that’s what their father Jacob told them. He gave each of them a unique and personal blessing as his final goodbye.

Then he gave them instructions: “Look, I’m about to die. Bury me with my ancestors in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite. It’s the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre in Canaan. Abraham bought that field as a burial plot. Abraham and Sarah are buried there, Isaac and Rebekah are buried there, and I buried Leah there too. The field and the cave were bought from the Hittites, so it’s legit.”
After Jacob finished telling his sons what to do, he pulled his feet up into bed, took his last breath, and passed away.

title: Joseph's Final Act: Forgiveness and a Promise
paragraphs: Joseph just broke down. He threw himself on his father, cried his eyes out, and kissed him goodbye.
§ Saying Goodbye to Dad

Then, Joseph told the doctors who worked for him to get his dad’s body ready for burial, Egyptian-style. So they embalmed Jacob, which took the full 40 days. The whole country of Egypt mourned for him for 70 days straight.

When the official mourning time was over, Joseph went to Pharaoh's officials and said, “Hey, if you guys think I’m cool, could you do me a solid and pass this message to Pharaoh? My dad made me promise him something super serious. He said, ‘Look, I’m about to die. You have to bury me in the tomb I got ready for myself back in Canaan.’ So, can you please let me go and bury my dad? I’ll come right back, for real.”
Pharaoh was like, “Of course. Go bury your father, just like you promised him.”
§ The Long Road to Canaan

So Joseph headed out to bury his father. And it was a huge deal. All of Pharaoh’s top advisors, all the big shots in Egypt, they all went with him. Joseph’s whole family went too—his brothers and everyone. They just left their kids and their animals back in Goshen. They even had chariots and horsemen with them. It was a massive funeral procession, like something out of a movie.

When they got to the Atad Threshing Floor, which is just across the Jordan River, they stopped and had a huge mourning ceremony. It was super loud and went on for a while. For seven days, Joseph led these funeral rituals for his dad.

The local Canaanites saw all this intense grieving and were like, “Whoa, the Egyptians are mourning like crazy.” That’s actually how that place got its name: Abel Mizraim, which means “Egyptian Mourning.”

Jacob’s sons did exactly what their dad told them to do. They carried him into Canaan and buried him in the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre. This was the same field Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite as a burial spot.
§ Brothers Get Scared

After the funeral, Joseph and his brothers and everyone who came with them went back to Egypt. But once they were back, his brothers started freaking out. They were talking to each other like, “Uh oh. What if Joseph is still holding a grudge? What if he decides to get us back for all the messed-up stuff we did to him?”

So they sent a message to Joseph that said, “Yo, before he died, our dad told us to tell you this: ‘Please, forgive your brothers for the terrible thing they did to you. It was really bad.’ So, will you? Can you forgive us? We’re all servants of the same God your father worshipped.”
When Joseph read their message, he started crying.
Then his brothers came to him in person, bowed down flat on the ground, and said, “We’ll be your slaves. For real.”
§ Joseph's Big Speech

But Joseph told them, “Chill out, guys. Don’t be scared. Do I look like God to you? Look, you totally planned to do something evil to me, but God flipped it and used your plan for something good. And the result is right in front of you—all these people are alive because of it. So seriously, don’t worry. You have nothing to be afraid of. I’ll take care of you and your kids.” He talked to them from the heart and made them feel a lot better.
§ The End of an Era

Joseph stayed in Egypt with his whole family and lived to be 110 years old. He got to see his great-grandkids from his son Ephraim. And the kids of his grandson Makir (from his other son Manasseh) were also considered part of his family.

When he knew his time was up, Joseph said to his brothers, “I’m about to die. But God is definitely going to come through for you. He’ll lead you out of this country and take you back to the land he promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
Then Joseph made them all swear an oath: “When God shows up to get you, you have to promise me you’ll take my bones with you when you leave.”
Joseph died when he was 110. They embalmed him and put him in a coffin in Egypt.
